en/forms/1-getting-started/01-why-this-p.title: 1.1 – Why this plugin
en/forms/1-getting-started/01-why-this-p.content:
Quartz builds a static website from notes: HTML files a web server hands out without computing
anything. A form, though, needs someone to take what was typed and pass it on. The website itself
cannot.
Three usual ways out





















WayWhat happensA form service (Formspree, Web3Forms …)The service takes the input and mails it on. It sees everything the visitor writes, and their address.A mail link (mailto:)The visitor’s mail program opens. Whoever has none set up gets no further.An embedded third-party formA frame from Google, Microsoft or another provider, with their look and their privacy.
What quartz-forms does differently

The forms belong to the website. They are generated at build time from
quartz.config.yaml, look like the rest of the page and speak its language.
Checking happens in the browser, when a field is left and when sending, in sentences rather
than error codes. The build checks the same rules before, the relay after.
Encryption happens in the browser. With OpenPGP only an encrypted block leaves the page. The
server that passes it on cannot read it.
Delivery goes through your own web space. The bundled relay is a single PHP file. It knows
the recipients’ addresses; the website only a name for them.
A form can be anonymous, and the code keeps the promise: no required personal details, no
reply address, no log.

Form services and mailto: remain possible as transports, for a website without PHP
(5.1).
What it is not

No database. A submission becomes a mail. Whoever wants to analyse answers analyses mails.
No file attachments. A form takes text, numbers, choices and a public PGP key, but no files.
No server. The relay is a script for classic web hosting with PHP, not a service someone
runs.

What you need

A website with Quartz 5.
For the relay, web space with PHP 8.1 or later and the mbstring extension; nearly every
host has both. Without PHP it works through a form service or mailto:.
For encrypted forms, a public PGP key, for instance from gpg, Thunderbird or Mailvelope.

en/forms/1-getting-started/02-the-first-.title: 1.2 – The first form
en/forms/1-getting-started/02-the-first-.content:
Four steps, and the form is on the page.
1. Install the plugin
npx quartz plugin add github:boxi-os/quartz-forms
The command fetches the plugin and adds it to quartz.config.yaml, with every option and its
default. The long list may be shortened: whatever is not written, the plugin takes as its default.
In QuartzControl the same goes through the
marketplace.
2. Describe the form
plugins:
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-forms
    enabled: true
    options:
      transport:
        kind: relay
        url: example.org/forms/send.php
      forms:
        first-form:
          title: A first form
          recipient: owner
          fields:
            - { type: text, name: name, label: Name, autocomplete: name }
            - { type: email, name: email, label: E-mail, autocomplete: email }
            - { type: textarea, name: message, label: Message, required: true }

forms holds every form of the website, each under an id of lower-case letters, digits and
hyphens. A page embeds the form by this id.
fields are the fields in their order (2.1).
transport says where a submission goes. Here it is the relay on your own web space
(5.2); recipient is the name the relay maps to an address.

To try things out first, write transport: { kind: demo }. The form then sends nothing and shows
what would have arrived, as here in the handbook.
3. Embed it
On any page, as a code block holding the id:
```quartz-form
first-form
```
The other ways (placeholder, frontmatter, layout) are in chapter 3.
4. Look at it
npx quartz build --serve
This is the result:

Sending it empty shows the checks in the browser. With a message, the form shows what would have
been sent.
When something is wrong

























What you seeWhyThe code block appears as code on the pageThe plugin is not in the config or enabled: false, or codeBlockLang is changed (3.1).The build stops: embeds the form "…", which options.forms does not haveThe id in the code block is not under forms. With --serve a note appears on the page instead.The build stops: [forms] 2 problem(s) in the quartz-forms optionsA description is wrong; the lines below name the path and the reason (9.2).The form says “The message could not be sent. Please try again later.”The target cannot be reached or refuses. When the relay refuses, the browser console names the code (5.3).

en/forms/1-getting-started/03-what-happe.title: 1.3 – What happens at build time
en/forms/1-getting-started/03-what-happe.content:
quartz-forms is a plugin of four parts. Each has one job, and together they turn an entry in the
config into a form that works in the browser.
1. The options are read and checked
Quartz hands the plugin the options from quartz.config.yaml. The plugin adds the defaults, lays
templates underneath (2.1) and checks every form: id, field names,
options, conditions, steps, transport, keys.

A problem stops the build. The message names the path in the config, such as
forms.contact.fields[2]: unknown field type "textfield".
A hint goes to the log, and the build carries on. It says what has no effect or works
differently from what was probably meant.

All messages are in 9.2.
2. The pages get their forms
The transformer looks for code blocks, placeholders and the frontmatter key on every page
(chapter 3) and puts the finished HTML form in their place: fields, labels,
hints and, invisible, the rules as JSON for the script in the browser. The component does the
same for the form that stands on every page through the layout
(3.4).
The page decides which language a form speaks (7.1).
3. The keys are checked and the encryption copied
The emitter checks every public key a form encrypts to: readable, public, not revoked, not
expired, able to encrypt. It writes the fingerprint to the log:
[forms] key "demo": 3EEC 26B0 22A0 0814 0EAF 4AD0 9FED 4B8B 67FD D91B (quartz-forms Demo …)

When at least one form encrypts, it copies OpenPGP.js to static/quartz-forms/openpgp/. The browser
loads it only on pages that need it.
4. In the browser
A script takes over every form on the page: it shows only the fields whose conditions hold and one
step at a time (chapter 4), checks when a field is left and when sending, sets
the spam traps (6.3), encrypts and sends. Without JavaScript an ordinary
HTML form remains (4.3).
What does not reach the website
The recipients’ addresses. They are only in the relay’s configuration on the web space; the website
sends the form’s id along, and the relay looks the address up. How that configuration is generated
from quartz.config.yaml is in 5.2.

en/forms/2-fields/01-field-types.title: 2.1 – Field types
en/forms/2-fields/01-field-types.content:
A form is a list of fields under fields. Every field has a type and a name, nearly every one a
label.

What every field has





































KeyMeaningtypeThe field type, see below.nameA letter, then letters, digits, _ or -; unique in the form. The value arrives under this name.labelThe label, a text. Required except for hidden and consent.requiredtrue makes the field required (2.2).hintA sentence below the field.widthfull, half or third (2.3).showIfShows the field only under a condition (4.1).
A text is either a string or a mapping of language to string:
label: { de: Nachricht, en: Message }. The page’s language picks
(7.1).
Some names belong to the submission itself and are closed to fields: form, lang, page,
pageTitle, ts, pow, captcha, encrypted, ciphertext, fields,
cf-turnstile-response, h-captcha-response, and anything beginning with _.
The types





















































































typeWhat it isOwn keystextOne line of textplaceholder, autocomplete, pattern, maxLengthemailAn e-mail addresslike texttelA phone numberlike texturlA web address with http:// or https://like textnumberA number; a comma counts as the decimal markmin, max, step, placeholderdateA date from the browser’s calendarautocomplete (such as bday); it takes placeholder and maxLength, but Chrome neither shows nor checks them on a datetextareaSeveral linesrows, placeholder, pattern, maxLengthselectOne choice from a drop-down listoptionsradioOne choice from visible optionsoptions, layoutcheckboxesSeveral choicesoptions, layoutcheckboxA single tick; ticked, yes arrives–scaleA step between two ends, at most 21 stepsmin, max (integers), minLabel, maxLabelconsentA consent, always requiredtext, link, linkLabelpgpKeyThe visitor’s public PGP key, pasted or as a fileat most one per formhiddenA fixed value the visitor does not seevalue
pageBreak is not a field but begins a step (4.2).
Options are a list of value and label:
- type: radio
  name: reply
  label: { de: Wie sollen wir antworten?, en: How should we reply? }
  options:
    - { value: email, label: { de: Per E-Mail, en: By e-mail } }
    - { value: phone, label: { de: Per Telefon, en: By phone } }
What arrives is the value, what is shown the label. The mail carries the labels, so nobody
has to look the values up.
A few details

autocomplete tells the browser what it may suggest (name, email, tel …). The relay
sets the mail’s reply address (Reply-To) to the first filled-in email field. When there are
several, such as your own address and a friend’s, the visitor’s gets autocomplete: email; then
only such fields count.
consent needs a text. link adds a link, to the privacy policy for instance, and
linkLabel names it.
pgpKey takes a public key. When the field is left, the browser checks it and names its
fingerprint; it refuses a private key. What it is good for is in
6.2.
hidden goes along with every submission, for instance to tell two forms with the same
fields apart.

Templates
Four field sets come with the plugin: contact, feedback, rsvp and survey.
forms:
  contact:
    template: contact
A template brings a title, fields and settings. Whatever the form states itself lies on top; own
fields replace the template’s fields entirely. What each template holds is shown in the recipes:
contact, feedback,
survey. rsvp is a sign-up with name, e-mail, date, number of people,
note and consent.

en/forms/2-fields/02-required-fields-and.title: 2.2 – Required fields and rules
en/forms/2-fields/02-required-fields-and.content:
A field’s rules are written once, in its description. They are applied three times: at build time,
in the browser and in the relay.

The rules








































KeyApplies toEffectrequired: trueevery fieldEmpty is not sent. consent is always required.maxLengthtext fieldsMost characters. Without it, spam.maxFieldLength (2000) applies to a line and spam.maxTextareaLength (20,000) to a text area.min, maxnumber, scaleThe smallest and the largest number.patterntext, textarea, email, tel, urlA regular expression the whole value must match.Typeemail, url, tel, number, dateAn e-mail address, an http(s) address, a phone number of digits, spaces and +()./-, a number, a day that exists.Optionsselect, radio, checkboxesOnly values that are in options.
Whitespace at the start and the end does not count. A field of nothing but spaces is empty.
When the browser checks

When a field is left, as soon as something is in it or a required field stays empty. The
sentence stands below the field and goes once the value is right.
When sending, every field that counts. Below the button it then says “Please check 3
field(s).”, and the focus jumps to the first one.

The sentences speak the page’s language:





































CaseSentenceRequired field empty“This field is required.”No option chosen“Please choose one option.” / “Please choose at least one option.”Consent missing“Please agree before sending.”Too long“Please use at most 200 characters.”Number out of range“Please enter 1 or more.” / “Please enter 8 or less.”Pattern missed“Please use the requested format.”Wrong format“Please enter a valid e-mail address.” and likewise for web address, phone number, number, date
Each of these sentences can be replaced (7.1). Since
“Please use the requested format.” does not say which, every pattern wants a hint.
Patterns
pattern is a regular expression in JavaScript notation. It has to match the whole value; ^
and $ may be there but are not needed.
- type: text
  name: zip
  label: Postcode
  pattern: "^[0-9]{5}$"
  hint: Five digits.
The relay checks the same pattern in PHP, that is with PCRE. Both read nearly everything alike, but
not everything. What only JavaScript knows, the build refuses: \u escapes, [^], [], a
lookbehind of unlimited length. What your own machine’s PCRE cannot read, generating the relay
configuration reports (5.2). Simple patterns of character classes
and repetitions are the safest.
Who else checks

The build checks the description: whether min is below max, whether every option has a
value, whether a pattern is a regular expression. An error stops the build
(9.2).
The relay checks every submission again by the same rules, because a browser can be
bypassed. When it refuses a field, the browser shows the sentence below exactly that field. An
encrypted submission the relay cannot read; it then only checks that it is a PGP block of the
allowed size.

en/forms/2-fields/03-width-and-arrangeme.title: 2.3 – Width and arrangement
en/forms/2-fields/03-width-and-arrangeme.content:
Without a setting, every field spans the whole width of the form, one below the other. Two keys
change that.

width





















ValueWidthfullThe whole row (default).halfHalf the row. Two fields stand side by side.thirdA third. Three fields stand side by side.
fields:
  - { type: text, name: first, label: First name, width: half }
  - { type: text, name: last, label: Last name, width: half }
  - { type: text, name: zip, label: Postcode, width: third }
  - { type: text, name: city, label: Town, width: third }
  - { type: text, name: country, label: Country, width: third }
Fields that do not fit the row start a new one. A half beside a third therefore leaves a gap.
The width follows the form, not the window. A form in a narrow column is narrow on a large
screen too. Below 32rem a third becomes a half; below 22rem every field spans the whole row again.
On a phone that gives one column by itself.
This needs container queries (Chrome 105, Safari 16, Firefox 110). An older browser shows every
field across the whole row.
layout: inline
For radio and checkboxes, layout: inline puts the options side by side. They wrap where the
row runs out.
- type: radio
  name: reply
  label: Reply by
  layout: inline
  options:
    - { value: email, label: E-mail }
    - { value: phone, label: Phone }
    - { value: post, label: Post }
For select it has no effect; its options are a drop-down list anyway. The build says so.

en/forms/3-embedding/01-code-block.title: 3.1 – Code block
en/forms/3-embedding/01-code-block.content:
The usual way: a code block in the language quartz-form with the id as its only line.
Questions about the course? Write to us:
 
```quartz-form
contact
```
After the build the form stands in its place. In Obsidian it stays a code block, and the note stays
readable.
Details

Only the first non-empty line counts. It is the id; nothing below it is read.
The same form twice on a page works. The second one’s fields get their own id attributes;
labels and errors stay with their form.
A language other than quartz-form is set with codeBlockLang, for instance when another
plugin needs the same name:

options:
  codeBlockLang: webform
Writing about the form
To show on a page what the code block looks like without it being replaced, wrap it in an outer
block of four backticks with the language markdown, as on this page. The inner block is then text
in a code block, not a code block of its own.

en/forms/3-embedding/02-placeholder.title: 3.2 – Placeholder
en/forms/3-embedding/02-placeholder.content:
{{form:id}} embeds a form where the placeholder stands.
If you want to come along, sign up here:
 
{{form:signup}}
Where the form lands

When the placeholder stands alone in its paragraph, the form replaces the paragraph.
When it is in the middle of text, it disappears from the sentence and the form follows the
paragraph. A form inside a paragraph would not be valid HTML.

Spaces inside the braces are allowed: {{ form:signup }} works the same.
When the placeholder beats the code block

In a callout, a table or another place where Obsidian shows no code block.
In text that comes from another tool and knows no code blocks.

What is not a placeholder
In code, that is between backticks or in a code block, {{form:signup}} stays as it is. That is how
a page can write about the placeholder, like this one.

en/forms/3-embedding/03-frontmatter.title: 3.3 – Frontmatter
en/forms/3-embedding/03-frontmatter.content:
A key in the frontmatter appends a form to the end of the page.
---
title: Contact
form: contact
---
This page carries form: first-form; the form therefore stands below the last paragraph.
Several forms, and none





















ValueEffectform: contactThe form contact at the end of the page.form: [contact, feedback]Both, in this order.form: falseNo additional form, and the form from the layout (3.4) is missing on this page.
When this fits
When the form belongs to the page and not to a place in the text: a “Contact” page whose text only
explains who answers. In Obsidian the note then holds no code block, just one line of frontmatter.
Another key
frontmatterKey changes the name, for instance when form already means something else:
options:
  frontmatterKey: webform
That then also applies to webform: false.

en/forms/3-embedding/04-layout.title: 3.4 – Layout
en/forms/3-embedding/04-layout.content:
A form that should stand on every page does not belong in every note but in the layout. The
plugin’s entry names it under layoutForm and says with layout where it goes:
plugins:
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-forms
    enabled: true
    options:
      layoutForm: feedback
      forms:
        feedback:
          template: feedback
    layout:
      position: afterBody
      priority: 20
layout is not part of the plugin but Quartz’s mechanism for every component: position is the
area (afterBody below the text, right in the right column …), priority the order within it.
Details

One layout form per entry. layoutForm names exactly one id; empty means none.
Hide it on single pages with form: false in the frontmatter (3.3).
The language is the page’s with language: auto. A fixed code such as language: en makes
the form speak the same language on every page.
Page context: the layout form knows the page it stands on. With pageContext: true its title
goes into the message, as in the feedback recipe
(8.2).
The form stands in a div.quartz-form-box, through which it can be styled on its own
(7.2).

In a side column
A form in the left or right column is narrow. The field widths follow the form, not the window
(2.3); two half fields stack there as soon as it gets
narrower than 22rem.
In QuartzControl the layout form is chosen in the “Forms” tab and placed in the layout editor like
any other component.

en/forms/3-embedding/index.title: 3 – Embedding
en/forms/3-embedding/index.content:
A form is described once under options.forms and then embedded, as often and wherever you like.
Four ways:






























WayWhenPageCode blockThe form stands at a particular place in the text.3.1Placeholder {{form:…}}Like the code block, but in running text or where a code block does not work.3.2FrontmatterThe form belongs to the page, not to a place in it.3.3LayoutThe same form on every page, such as feedback below the text.3.4
The transformer replaces the first three with the finished form at build time; the fourth is a
component in the layout. When a page names an id that does not exist, the build stops; with
--serve a note appears on the page instead.

en/forms/4-flow/01-conditions.title: 4.1 – Conditions
en/forms/4-flow/01-conditions.content:
showIf shows a field only while an earlier field has one of the named values.

fields:
  - type: radio
    name: reply
    label: How should we reply?
    required: true
    options:
      - { value: email, label: By e-mail }
      - { value: phone, label: By phone }
      - { value: none, label: Not at all }
  - { type: email, name: email, label: E-mail, required: true, showIf: { field: reply, equals: email } }
  - { type: tel, name: phone, label: Phone, required: true, showIf: { field: reply, equals: phone } }
The rule
showIf: { field, equals }

field names a field that comes before it and is a select, radio, checkboxes,
checkbox or scale. No condition hangs on a text field.
equals is one value or a list of them: an option value, yes for a ticked checkbox, for a
scale the number as text ("5"). For checkboxes it is enough when one of the values is ticked.

A field has at most one condition. Several cases go through the list: equals: [email, phone].
Chains
Conditions may build on each other. In the form above, “I have an order number” appears only for an
order, and the field for the number only when the box is ticked:
  - type: select
    name: topic
    label: What is it about?
    options:
      - { value: question, label: A question }
      - { value: order, label: An order }
  - { type: checkbox, name: hasNumber, label: I have an order number, showIf: { field: topic, equals: order } }
  - { type: text, name: orderNumber, label: Order number, required: true, showIf: { field: hasNumber, equals: "yes" } }
When the topic goes back to “A question”, both disappear: a field whose controlling field does
not count does not count either, whatever is in it.
What “does not count” means
A field whose condition does not hold

is not required, even with required: true,
is not checked,
is not sent and is not in the mail.

Whatever the visitor typed into it before stays in the field and is back when the condition holds
again. When a tampered browser sends a value anyway, the relay drops it without refusing the
submission.
What cannot be conditional

hidden: a fixed value always goes along.
consent: a consent that can disappear would be none. The same goes for a step with a
condition (4.2).

Without JavaScript
Without the script every field is there. A conditional one then carries no required, and a
sentence below it says when it is needed: “Only needed if “How should we reply?” is “By e-mail”.”
The relay decides by the same rules which fields count.
What the build refuses
A field that does not exist or comes later, a controlling field of the wrong type, and a value the
controlling field cannot have. The messages are in 9.2.

en/forms/4-flow/02-steps.title: 4.2 – Steps
en/forms/4-flow/02-steps.content:
An entry type: pageBreak in fields begins a new step. The visitor then sees one section at a
time, with “Next” and “Back”.

fields:
  - { type: text, name: name, label: Name, required: true }
  - { type: email, name: email, label: E-mail, required: true }
  - { type: pageBreak, title: Attendance }
  - type: radio
    name: attend
    label: Are you coming?
    required: true
    options:
      - { value: "yes", label: "Yes" }
      - { value: "no", label: "No" }
  - { type: pageBreak, title: Details, showIf: { field: attend, equals: "yes" } }
  - { type: number, name: guests, label: How many people?, min: 1, max: 6, required: true }
  - { type: pageBreak, title: Finish }
  - { type: textarea, name: note, label: Anything else? }
  - { type: consent, name: consent, text: I agree that … }
What the visitor sees

Above the step it says “Step 2 of 4: Attendance”. When a step has no title, the part after
the colon is missing.
“Next” checks only the fields of the open step. Return in a field works like “Next”.
“Back” goes back without checking; what is filled in stays.
Encryption, captcha and “Send” appear only with the last step.
When the relay refuses a field, the form opens the step it is in.

A step with a condition
A pageBreak can carry a showIf. When it does not hold, the step is skipped both ways, and the
count counts only the steps that count: whoever picks “No” above sees “Step 3 of 3: Finish” instead
of “4 of 4”. A step in which no field counts is skipped the same way.
The step’s condition applies to every one of its fields. That is why a consent cannot stand in a
step with a condition: if the step were skipped, the message would go without it. The build
refuses that. A hidden value in such a step goes along anyway.
Where a break may stand
Between fields; not first, not last and not twice in a row. A step that holds only hidden values
shows the visitor nothing; the build says so.
Without JavaScript
All steps stand one below the other, each under its title, with a single “Send” button at the end.

en/forms/4-flow/03-without-javascript.title: 4.3 – Without JavaScript
en/forms/4-flow/03-without-javascript.content:
A form of quartz-forms is an ordinary HTML form first. The script makes it more comfortable and
safer, but not every form needs it to send.
Who can send without the script

































FormWithout JavaScriptencryption: off or optional, relay, noScript: true (default)A plain form post to the relay. It answers with the redirect from success or a short page in the submission’s language. Refused fields it names with the same sentences as the script.encryption: requiredNo target, the button stays disabled. A note says: “This form sends encrypted and needs JavaScript to do so.”noScript: falseNo target, the button stays disabled: “This form needs JavaScript to send.”endpoint, formspree, web3formsA plain post to the service; the answer page comes from there.mailtoThe mail program opens with the fields as text.demoNo target. Without the script there is nothing to demonstrate: “This demonstration needs JavaScript to show what would have been sent.” (from quartz-forms 0.5.6 on)
With encryption: optional the “Send encrypted” box stays empty and disabled without the script,
and a note says: “Without JavaScript this form sends unencrypted.” Only the script can encrypt; a
post that carries the box anyway, the relay refuses.
What looks different

Conditional fields are all there, each with a sentence saying when it is needed
(4.1).
Steps stand one below the other (4.2).
Checking covers only what the browser can do itself: required, type, pattern,
maxlength. The relay checks the rest.
A pgpKey field takes the pasted text; choosing a file works only with the script.

What is weaker without the script
A plain post carries neither the time stamp nor the proof of work that the script fetches from the
relay when the page opens (6.3). The relay checks only the honeypot,
the rate limit and the fields on it. Whoever sets pow: true or their own minSeconds and leaves
noScript: true gets a hint at build time. noScript: false closes the gap and in exchange takes
the form away from visitors without JavaScript.
A website with Referrer-Policy: no-referrer hides its origin in a plain post, and the relay
refuses it (5.3). The script’s requests are not
affected.

en/forms/5-sending/01-the-transports-com.title: 5.1 – The transports compared
en/forms/5-sending/01-the-transports-com.content:
transport says where a submission goes. It is set once for every form under options, and each
form can override single keys of it:
options:
  transport:
    kind: relay
    url: example.org/forms/send.php
  forms:
    contact:
      template: contact
      recipient: owner
    newsletter:
      transport:
        kind: formspree
        url: xyzabcde
      fields: [ … ]
The six ways















































kindWhere tourlRecipientrelayquartz-forms’ PHP script on your own web space (5.2)the address of send.phprecipient: a name the relay maps to an addressendpointAny address that takes a POSTthe addressset up at the endpointformspreeFormspreeFormspree’s form idset up at Formspreeweb3formsWeb3Formsthe Web3Forms access keyset up at Web3FormsmailtoThe visitor’s mail program–recipient: the address itselfdemoNowhere; the form shows what would have arrived––
What each can do





























































relayendpoint, servicesmailtodemoAddress stays off the websiteyesyesno, it is in the link–Encryption in the browseryesyes, the ciphertext arrives in the field messageyes, the whole ciphertext is in the mailyes, it is shownChecking on the serveryes, every rulewhatever the service checksnonoTime trapmeasured by the relayin the browser onlyin the browser onlynoneProof of work, rate limityesnononoAnonymousyesthe service sees the sender’s addressno–Without JavaScriptplain postplain postmail programno
The build says what has no effect with the chosen way: pow and rateLimitPerHour without the
relay, extra with the relay, an anonymous form through a service
(9.2).
When to use which

relay when the web space has PHP. Only then does everything stay in your hands, and only
then do all the protections in 6.3 work.
formspree or web3forms when there is no PHP and a service is fine. With encryption it sees
only the ciphertext (8.6).
endpoint for another service or a script of your own that takes JSON or a form post.
mailto for the simplest case without any server, at the price that the address is on the
website and a visitor without a mail program gets no further.
demo for trying things out and for pages like these, which show a form without anyone
receiving it.

The endpoint in detail





















KeyMeaningurlThe address that is posted to.formatjson (default) or form for an ordinary form post.extraFields that go along with every submission, such as an access key: extra: { apikey: "…" }.
The fields arrive flat, under their names; several choices separated by commas. Along with them
_subject with the subject and, with pageContext, _page with the page. An encrypted submission
has a single field message with the PGP block instead of the fields.
The endpoint should best answer with JSON: { "ok": true } on success, otherwise a status outside
2xx and { "message": "…" }. The form then shows that sentence to the visitor; with
{ "errors": [{ "field": "email", "message": "…" }] } the sentences go below the fields.

en/forms/5-sending/02-the-relay.title: 5.2 – The relay
en/forms/5-sending/02-the-relay.content:
The relay is a single file, send.php, for classic web hosting with PHP 8.1 or later and the
mbstring extension. It takes what the website’s forms send, checks it again and passes it on as
a mail. It needs no packages.
Two configuration files




















FileContentsWhere fromconfig.generated.phpThe forms: ids, fields, rules, conditions, spam settings, the website’s base URLGenerated from quartz.config.yaml. Generate it again and upload it after every change to a form.config.phpWhat only the operator knows: the secret, the addressesWith the command line by hand: created once and never overwritten afterwards. With QuartzControl written anew on every upload from the values stored there; a change made by hand on the server then lasts only until the next upload.
config.php holds:













































KeyMeaningsecretAt least 32 random characters (openssl rand -base64 32). The relay signs time stamps and challenges with it.allowedOriginsThe website’s address, such as ['example.org']. The relay answers only requests from there.fromThe sender address of the mails, best one of your own domain.subjectPrefixOptional, before every subject, such as [Website].recipientsName → address, e.g. 'owner' => 'me@example.org'. The names are the forms’ recipient values.captchaSecretThe captcha provider’s secret key; per form through captchaSecrets.mailer'mail' (default), ['sendmail' => '/usr/sbin/sendmail -t -i'] or, for testing, ['file' => '/path/outbox.txt'].envelopeSendertrue (default): from also goes as the envelope sender (-f), so SPF checks its domain. false leaves it to the host, for one that refuses -f.counterDirWhere the counters live; best outside the web root.
The addresses never reach the website. A form names only a name with recipient: owner; which
address belongs to it, only config.php knows.
Generating it
From a website that has quartz-forms installed:
node .quartz/plugins/quartz-forms/dist/cli.js relay --site . --out relay
This writes the whole relay into the folder relay: send.php, config.generated.php,
counters/.htaccess and, the first time, config.php with a fresh secret. A second run renews
everything except config.php:
wrote relay/config.generated.php (1 form(s) on the relay)
relay/config.php kept (addresses and secret are yours)

Only forms with kind: relay are in config.generated.php. When php is installed on your own
machine, generating compiles every pattern the way the relay does and stops at one PHP cannot read
(2.2).
The same command line checks the forms without building, and names every key with its fingerprint:
node .quartz/plugins/quartz-forms/dist/cli.js check --site .
In QuartzControl the “Forms” tab generates the relay and uploads it through an existing publishing
target; the secret and the addresses are kept encrypted there.
What the relay checks
In this order, and every refusal has a code the browser turns into a sentence
(9.2):

Form: the id is in config.generated.php.
Size: at most spam.maxBytes.
Origin: the request comes from an address in allowedOrigins.
Honeypot: when the invisible field is filled in, the relay answers “sent” and sends nothing.
Time trap: the time stamp the relay signed when the page opened is old enough
(6.3).
Proof of work, when the form asks for it.
Fields: which fields count (4.1), then each by its rules. An
encrypted submission has to be exactly one PGP block.
Recipient: there is an address for the name.
Captcha, when the form has one, verified with the provider.
Rate limit: room left in the hour.

Then the mail goes out: UTF-8 text, with the form’s subject, From from config.php and, when the
form is not anonymous and the message not encrypted, Reply-To set to the visitor’s address.
Whether it arrives depends on the SPF and DKIM records of the domain in from.
What it promises
The relay logs nothing and stores no senders. The counters hold only how many messages a form got
in an hour. The host’s access log is outside this file.

en/forms/5-sending/03-the-relay-on-your-.title: 5.3 – The relay on your web space
en/forms/5-sending/03-the-relay-on-your-.content:
State of this page 
                  
                

The relay is checked by a test suite under php -S: every refusal, every accepted path, mails
into a file. On a real web space with Apache or nginx, with real mail delivery and an upload over
SFTP or FTP, it has not been measured yet. The steps below follow the code and its documentation.


1. Generate
node .quartz/plugins/quartz-forms/dist/cli.js relay --site . --out relay
What that creates is in 5.2.
2. Fill in config.php
'allowedOrigins' => ['example.org'],
'from' => 'forms@example.org',
'recipients' => [
    'owner' => 'me@example.org',
],
secret is set already. An address that still ends in @example. counts as missing; the relay
refuses that recipient’s forms.
3. Upload
send.php, config.php, config.generated.php and the folder counters/ with its .htaccess into
a folder of the web space, for instance example.org/forms/.

counters/ must be writable for PHP. Under Apache the .htaccess keeps the folder closed;
the relay writes it again when it is missing. nginx reads no .htaccess: deny the folder in
the server block there or, better, set counterDir in config.php to a folder outside the web
root.
config.php holds the secret and the addresses. After the upload, check that no other account
on the host can read it: 0600 where PHP runs as your own user (PHP-FPM, suEXEC), otherwise
0640 with the web server’s group. An upload over SFTP or FTP does not keep the permissions.
A test outbox (mailer => ['file' => …]) belongs outside the web root too, or every message
is one address away.

4. Point the website at it
options:
  transport:
    kind: relay
    url: example.org/forms/send.php
Build again and publish.
5. Test
With the form itself, or from the command line:
curl -i -X POST example.org/forms/send.php \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Origin: example.org' \
  -d '{"form":"contact","lang":"en","ts":0,"encrypted":false,"fields":{"message":"hello"}}'
With minSeconds above 0 the relay answers stamp: the stamp 0 is not its own. That shows the time
trap works. Without a time trap the mail arrives.
After every change to a form
Repeat step 1 and upload config.generated.php again. Otherwise the relay does not know a new
field and refuses submissions as unknown_field; the visitor reads “The message could not be sent.
Please try again later.”, and the browser console names the code.
When it does not work









































AnswerCause500 mbstring_configThe host’s PHP lacks the mbstring extension.500 secret_configsecret is missing, shorter than 32 characters or still the placeholder. It is asked for only when a time trap or a proof of work has something to sign.403 originThe website is not in allowedOrigins. Or it sends Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and a plain post without JavaScript hides its origin that way; the message says which of the two.404 unknown_formconfig.generated.php is older than the form.500 recipientThere is no address in config.php for the name in recipient.500 captcha_configcaptchaSecret is missing, or the host can reach the provider neither through allow_url_fopen nor through cURL.502 mailPHP could not hand the mail over. Check with the host whether mail() is allowed, or use sendmail. If the host refuses the envelope sender, 'envelopeSender' => false helps; the message says so.The mail does not arriveSPF or DKIM of the domain in from does not match the server. If the relay answers ok, a sendmail may also have dropped the mail over -f: try 'envelopeSender' => false.

en/forms/6-protection/01-anonymous.title: 6.1 – Anonymous
en/forms/6-protection/01-anonymous.content:
anonymous: true turns a form into one that asks nothing about the sender and passes nothing about
them on, unless they write it in themselves.

This form’s description asks for an e-mail address (required: true). Because it is anonymous, the
plugin makes the field optional and says at build time:
forms.anonymous.fields[0]: anonymous, so "email" (email) cannot be required and is made optional

What the code enforces

No required personal details. email, tel, pgpKey and fields whose autocomplete names
a person (name, given-name, street-address …) become optional.
No page context. pageContext has no effect; which page the visitor was reading does not go
along.
No reply address. The relay sets no Reply-To.
No third-party captcha. A widget would hand the visitor’s address to the provider; an
anonymous form loads none, and the relay asks for no token.
No log in the relay.

Above the form it says: “This form is anonymous: nothing identifies you unless you write it.”
What nobody can promise

The host’s access log. The web server the relay runs on can record every request with address
and time. That is outside the relay.
The network in between. Whoever sees the visitor’s network sees that they visit the website.
A form service. Formspree and Web3Forms see the address of every submission; the build warns
about that combination.
What the visitor writes. A name in the message is a name.

Together with encryption
Anonymous does not mean encrypted. Whoever wants both writes both; the recipe
8.5 shows such a form. A visitor’s key for a reply (pgpKey) is
then optional, and its hint should say that a key carrying a name gives the name away.

en/forms/6-protection/02-encryption.title: 6.2 – Encryption
en/forms/6-protection/02-encryption.content:
An encrypting form puts the message together in the visitor’s browser and encrypts it there with
OpenPGP for the listed public keys. Only the encrypted block leaves the page. Whoever has the
matching private key can read it.

Adding keys
The public keys are listed once under keys, each under a name:
options:
  keys:
    owner:
      file: keys/owner.asc
    team:
      armored: |
        -----BEGIN PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----
        …
        -----END PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----

file is a path relative to the website’s folder and must lie inside it.
armored is the key itself, as text.

A public key is exported with gpg --export --armor me@example.org, for instance. The build refuses a
private key.
Encrypting a form
forms:
  contact:
    template: contact
    encryption:
      mode: optional
      keys: [owner]





















modeEffectoffUnencrypted (default).optionalA “Send encrypted” box, ticked as soon as the script runs. The visitor can untick it. Without JavaScript the message goes unencrypted (4.3).requiredNothing goes out unencrypted. Without JavaScript the form cannot send.
keys names entries of keys; without it, all of them. With several keys each of them can read the
message. showFingerprint: false hides the line with the fingerprint below the form.
What the build checks
Every key a form encrypts to: readable, public, not revoked, not expired, with a subkey that can
encrypt. A problem stops the build. It writes the fingerprint to the log, so you can compare it with
your own.
Below the form the same fingerprint appears: “Encrypted in your browser for the key 3EEC 26B0 …”.
Publishing it elsewhere too, on a contact page for instance, lets visitors compare.
What the message holds
One line Label: value per field (for a text area the value in the lines below), a tick as [x] or
[ ], with pageContext a line Page: title (slug) at the end, and, when the visitor gave a key of
their own, that key under Public key of the sender:. Exactly this text is encrypted. The two fixed
lines are in the page’s language; on a German page they read Seite: and Öffentlicher Schlüssel des Absenders:.
The mail can be read with gpg --decrypt, Thunderbird, Mailvelope or GPG Suite.
The visitor’s key
A field of type pgpKey takes the visitor’s public key, pasted or as a file. The browser checks it
when the field is left and names its fingerprint: “Key accepted, fingerprint …”. With it you can
reply encrypted. For an encrypted message the relay sets no Reply-To; the visitor’s address, if
they gave it, is in the encrypted text.
What encryption does not protect

Scripts on the same page. What the visitor types is plain text in the fields until they send.
Any script on the page can read it: a captcha provider’s widget (the build says so for an
encrypting form with captcha), Quartz’s analytics, another plugin’s script.
What travels in the clear: the form’s id, the page’s language, the time stamp, that the
message is encrypted, and how large. The mail carries the form’s subject. A service (endpoint,
formspree, web3forms) gets the subject as _subject, the extra fields and a captcha’s token
beside the ciphertext; the page stays inside it (from 0.5.5 on; before, it travelled as _page).

When OpenPGP cannot be loaded
A content blocker, a broken connection or a strict content security policy can prevent loading. An
encrypting form then says: “Encryption could not be loaded; the message was not sent.” A form that
does not encrypt still sends; a pasted key then goes along unchecked, and the field says so.
Decrypting the demonstration yourself
The forms of this handbook encrypt to a key that exists only for demonstrating. Its private part is
here so you can check that the output really is encrypted. It protects nothing and is good for
nothing else.


                  
                  Private key of the demonstration 
                  
                

Import it with gpg --import demo.asc, copy a form’s output into a file and run
gpg --decrypt message.asc.

en/forms/6-protection/03-spam.title: 6.3 – Spam
en/forms/6-protection/03-spam.content:
Every form has spam protection, and most of it needs no third-party service. It is set under
spam, globally for every form or per form for single keys:
options:
  spam:
    pow: true
  forms:
    contact:
      template: contact
      spam:
        minSeconds: 5
The means



























































KeyDefaultWhat it doesWorks withhoneypottrueAn invisible field a human leaves empty. When it is filled in, the form says “sent” and sends nothing.every wayminSeconds3Least time between opening and sending, in whole seconds. 0 switches it off.in the browser for every way but demo; measured again only by the relaynoScripttrueAllow sending without JavaScript (4.3). With false the form has no target without the script, and the relay refuses plain posts.every waypowfalseA computing task before every message.the relaypowDifficulty16Its difficulty in bits, 8 to 20.the relaycaptchanoneturnstile or hcaptcha.the relay and the servicescaptchaSiteKey""The provider’s public key.rateLimitPerHour60Most mails per form and hour.the relay
What has no effect without the relay, the build says (“has no effect without the relay”).
Time trap
A bot fills in a form in a fraction of a second. When the page opens, the script fetches a time
stamp from the relay, which the relay signs; when sending, the relay measures with its own clock
whether enough time has passed. A visitor’s clock that is off locks nobody out, a made-up stamp is
refused. When the stamp is older than a day or none came when the page opened, the script fetches a
new one, waits the time out and sends again.
Sent too fast, the visitor reads: “Please wait a moment before sending.” A form with demo sets
no time trap, because it sends nothing (from quartz-forms 0.5.6 on).
Proof of work
With pow: true the browser solves a computing task before every message, which the relay set and
checks in a fraction of a second. For a human it is a short pause; for someone who wants to send a
thousand messages, a thousand pauses. The computing happens in a worker; the page stays usable.

















powDifficultyDuration, roughly16up to a second on a desktop18–20seconds on a phone; the build says so
Every solution is good for one message. It is counted only when the message is accepted; a refused
submission does not cost the visitor a new one.
Captcha
spam:
  captcha: turnstile
  captchaSiteKey: 0x4AAAAAAA…
The Cloudflare Turnstile or hCaptcha widget appears above the send button; the provider’s secret
key goes into the relay’s config.php (5.2); with a service, the
service checks it itself.
Three things are worth knowing:

An anonymous form loads no captcha, because the widget shows the provider the visitor’s
address (6.1).
Nor does a form with demo: it sends nothing a captcha could protect (from quartz-forms
0.5.5 on).
The provider’s script runs on the page where the message is typed before it is encrypted, and
could read it. The build says so for an encrypting form with a captcha.

Rate limit
The relay counts per form how many mails it has sent in the current hour; when rateLimitPerHour is
reached, it takes nothing more until the hour is over. It stores no addresses for that.
This protects the mailbox, not the form. Because no addresses are counted, the limit is a quota
for everyone: a single client that sends the hour’s 60 mails itself (plain posts take less than a
second for that) closes the form to everyone else. Only a captcha, or a proof of work with
noScript: false that a plain post cannot skip, makes that costly. The build says so for every
relay form without either.
Size limits






























KeyDefaultLimitmaxFieldLength2000Characters of a one-line field without its own maxLengthmaxTextareaLength20000Characters of a text area without its own maxLengthmaxKeyLength16384Characters of a pasted keymaxBytes131072Bytes of a whole submission
When the fields together can hold more than maxBytes, the build says so, for an encrypting form
with the PGP block’s overhead. A smaller maxLength on the large fields helps.

en/forms/7-appearance/01-texts-and-langu.title: 7.1 – Texts and languages
en/forms/7-appearance/01-texts-and-langu.content:
A form speaks two kinds of text: what is in its description (title, labels, hints, options) and
what quartz-forms says itself (“Send”, “This field is required.”, “Step 2 of 4”).
Which language
The page’s: lang in the frontmatter, otherwise the website’s locale. With
quartz-multilanguage that plugin sets lang for
every page in a language folder, so a form on an English page speaks English without you doing
anything. This handbook is built that way.
The form in the layout (3.4) follows the page too with
language: auto; a fixed code such as language: en keeps it at one language.
Labels in several languages
Every text of a description is a string or a mapping of language to string:
- type: textarea
  name: message
  label: { de: Nachricht, en: Message }
  hint:
    de: Was du uns sagen willst.
    en: What you want to tell us.
The page’s full code (en-GB) is looked for first, then the language (en). When neither is there,
the form takes the first entry.
quartz-forms’ own sentences
German and English come with the plugin; any other language gets English. The German
sentences address the visitor with the informal “du”.
Every sentence can be replaced per language:
options:
  texts:
    en:
      submit: Submit
      sent: Thanks, we will get back to you.

The keys are in 9.1.
{min}, {max}, {count}, {field} and similar placeholders are filled in by the code; they
belong in the new sentence.
An unknown key, a placeholder left out or one the text does not have, or a language the plugin
has no sentences for, gives a hint at build time. The sentences apply all the same, as written;
that is how a third language gets its wording.

Formal German
Whoever wants the formal “Sie” in German replaces the sentences through texts and writes the
fields themselves instead of using a template; the templates use “du”. What cannot be replaced is
the short page the relay answers a plain post without JavaScript with; it keeps the informal form.
Subject and success

























KeyMeaningsubjectThe mail’s subject, a text. Without it, the title, otherwise the id.submitLabelThe send button’s caption for this one form.success.textThe sentence after sending, instead of “Thank you, your message has been sent.” With demo it is always the demonstration’s sentence (demoSent, encrypting demoSentEncrypted).success.mode: redirect with success.slugGo to a page of the website instead of showing a sentence. The build checks that the page exists. With demo the page stays where it is.

en/forms/7-appearance/02-css-variables.title: 7.2 – CSS variables
en/forms/7-appearance/02-css-variables.content:
quartz-forms brings a stylesheet. It takes colours and fonts from the Quartz theme’s variables, so
the form follows the website’s light and dark mode. Everything you might want to change is a CSS
variable on .quartz-form.
The variables




























































VariableDefaultWhat for--quartz-forms-gap1remSpace between the fields--quartz-forms-radius5pxRounding of fields and buttons--quartz-forms-bordervar(--lightgray)The fields’ border--quartz-forms-border-focusvar(--secondary)Focus ring--quartz-forms-field-bgvar(--light)The fields’ background--quartz-forms-error#b3261e, dark #f2b8b5Error sentences, the required asterisk, a wrong field’s border--quartz-forms-success#2e7d32, dark #a5d6a7The sentence after sending--quartz-forms-button-bgvar(--secondary)The send button’s background--quartz-forms-button-fgvar(--light)The send button’s text--quartz-forms-max-width40remThe form’s largest width
Changing them
In quartz/styles/custom.scss:
.quartz-form {
  --quartz-forms-radius: 0;
  --quartz-forms-max-width: 100%;
  --quartz-forms-button-bg: var(--tertiary);
}
quartz-forms’ stylesheet sits in Quartz’s cascade layer quartz-base. Every rule in custom.scss
is outside it and wins, however specific it is. (Up to 0.5.1 a second copy of the stylesheet reached
the page without a layer and beat such rules.) The same goes for a theme’s rules: one that styles the
article’s input, select, textarea, label, button, fieldset or pre styles the form’s
too, edge, ground, font size and the button’s colours. QuartzControl’s templates therefore style the
form themselves (below).
Two rules stand outside the layer on purpose. The first gives the form’s checkboxes and radios back
the browser’s look, so a theme that draws task lists with glyphs of its own does not catch them too.
The second takes the outer margin off the form’s paragraphs, headings and field groups, so the
theme’s rhythm for paragraphs (article p) leaves no gap under every hint; the spacing inside the
form comes from the variables above. Whoever wants otherwise writes a selector more specific than
.quartz-form input[type="checkbox"] or .quartz-form p, such as
form.quartz-form input[type="checkbox"] or .quartz-form .quartz-form__hint.
A single form
className gives a form extra classes:
forms:
  newsletter:
    className: compact
.quartz-form.compact {
  --quartz-forms-gap: 0.5rem;
}
Every form also carries its id: form.quartz-form[data-form="newsletter"]. The form from the layout
also stands in a div.quartz-form-box.
The field widths
The two limits at which thirds become halves and halves become whole rows (32rem and 22rem,
2.3) are numbers in the stylesheet, not variables:
container queries take no CSS variables.
This website
This handbook’s template maps every variable to one of its own tokens (a control’s edge, the focus
colour, the colours for errors and success) and gives fields and buttons the same height as its
other controls. QuartzControl’s templates bring this design along.

en/forms/8-recipes/01-contact.title: 8.1 – Contact
en/forms/8-recipes/01-contact.content:
The contact form most websites need.

options:
  transport:
    kind: relay
    url: example.org/forms/send.php
  keys:
    owner:
      file: keys/owner.asc
  forms:
    contact:
      template: contact
      recipient: owner
      encryption:
        mode: optional
        keys: [owner]
What the template brings
The template contact has the title “Contact” and four fields:






























FieldTypeNametext, autocomplete: nameE-mailemail, autocomplete: emailHint “Only if you want a reply.”MessagetextareaRequiredConsentconsent“I agree that my message is processed to answer it.”
All in English and German. Without encryption the relay sets Reply-To to the given address, so a
reply is one click.
Variations

Always encrypted: mode: required. Without JavaScript the form then cannot send.
With a link to the privacy policy: your own fields instead of the template, with
link: /privacy on the consent (2.1).
On a page of its own: form: contact in the contact page’s frontmatter
(3.3).
A thank-you page after sending: success: { mode: redirect, slug: thanks }.

en/forms/8-recipes/02-feedback-on-every-.title: 8.2 – Feedback on every page
en/forms/8-recipes/02-feedback-on-every-.content:
A short question below every text: was the page helpful? The message says which page it was about.

On this website the form stands only here, as a code block. On a real website it goes below every
text through the layout:
plugins:
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-forms
    enabled: true
    options:
      transport:
        kind: relay
        url: example.org/forms/send.php
      layoutForm: feedback
      forms:
        feedback:
          template: feedback
          recipient: owner
    layout:
      position: afterBody
      priority: 20
What the template brings
The title “Feedback on this page”, pageContext: true and two fields: a required scale from 1
(“Not at all”) to 5 (“Very”) and a text area “What could be better?”.
With pageContext, “Refers to the page “…”.” stands above the form, and the message ends with
Page: title (slug). Whoever sends sees that line in the output above.
Variations

Hide it on single pages, the home page for instance: form: false in the frontmatter.
On the right instead of below the text: position: right. The form gets narrow there; this
template’s fields stack anyway.
Anonymous: anonymous: true. Then the page does not go along and the feedback loses its
reference; better a field of your own with the page as a choice.

en/forms/8-recipes/03-sign-up.title: 8.3 – Sign-up
en/forms/8-recipes/03-sign-up.content:
A sign-up that asks only for what is needed: whoever declines is done after two clicks.

forms:
  signup:
    title: Sign-up for the summer party
    description: Saturday 12 July, from 4 pm in the garden.
    recipient: owner
    fields:
      - { type: text, name: name, label: Name, required: true, autocomplete: name, width: half }
      - { type: email, name: email, label: E-mail, required: true, autocomplete: email, width: half }
      - type: radio
        name: attend
        label: Are you coming?
        required: true
        layout: inline
        options:
          - { value: "yes", label: "Yes" }
          - { value: "no", label: Sadly not }
      - { type: pageBreak, title: Who is coming?, showIf: { field: attend, equals: "yes" } }
      - { type: number, name: guests, label: People in all, min: 1, max: 6, required: true, width: third }
      - type: checkboxes
        name: food
        label: We bring
        layout: inline
        options:
          - { value: salad, label: Salad }
          - { value: cake, label: Cake }
          - { value: drinks, label: Drinks }
      - { type: checkbox, name: kids, label: With children }
      - { type: number, name: kidsCount, label: How many children?, min: 1, max: 6, required: true, width: third, showIf: { field: kids, equals: "yes" } }
      - { type: pageBreak, title: Almost done }
      - { type: textarea, name: note, label: Note, rows: 3 }
      - type: consent
        name: consent
        text: I agree that my details are stored to organise the event.
How it fits together

Three steps, the middle one with a condition: whoever picks “Sadly not” jumps from step 1
straight to “Almost done”, and the count says “Step 2 of 2: Almost done”
(4.2).
A chain in the middle step: “How many children?” appears only with the “With children” box
ticked, and is required only then (4.1).
The consent in the last step, which has no condition. In a step with a condition the build
would refuse it.
"yes" and "no" in quotes: they are not needed, Quartz reads the config as YAML 1.2, where
a bare yes stays a word. Older YAML readers (YAML 1.1) make a boolean of it, though; in quotes
the value is the same everywhere.
Name and e-mail side by side, stacked on a phone (2.3).

The message
For an acceptance, for instance:
Name: Ada Lovelace
E-mail: ada@example.org
Are you coming?: Yes
People in all: 3
We bring: Salad, Cake
[x] With children
How many children?: 1
[x] I agree that my details are stored to organise the event.

For a refusal every line of the middle step is missing.

en/forms/8-recipes/04-survey.title: 8.4 – Survey
en/forms/8-recipes/04-survey.content:
A short survey among the readers, anonymous.

forms:
  survey:
    template: survey
    recipient: owner
    encryption:
      mode: optional
      keys: [owner]
What the template brings
The title “Survey”, anonymous: true and four fields: how often one visits the website (radio,
required), which topics are of interest (checkboxes), how satisfied one is (scale from 1 to 5)
and a free field “Anything else?”.
Because the survey is anonymous, the note saying so stands above the form, and neither the page nor
a reply address goes along (6.1).
Analysing
Every answer is a mail. quartz-forms adds nothing up; whoever wants results collects the mails. To
make that easier:

Fixed values instead of free fields where possible: options and scales can be counted.
A subject of its own (subject: Survey 2026), so a mailbox filter collects the answers.
Without encryption the mails can be read by a machine; with it, each has to be decrypted
first. For a survey without sensitive questions, mode: off is a reasonable choice.

Variations

A question only for regulars: showIf: { field: usage, equals: often } on another field.
Several pages: a pageBreak between the blocks of topics.

en/forms/8-recipes/05-anonymous-tip.title: 8.5 – Anonymous tip
en/forms/8-recipes/05-anonymous-tip.content:
For tips someone does not want to give under their name: no required personal field, nothing in
plain text on the way.

forms:
  tipoff:
    title: Send a tip
    description: Anonymous and encrypted. We only learn what you write.
    recipient: owner
    anonymous: true
    encryption:
      mode: required
      keys: [owner]
    fields:
      - type: select
        name: area
        label: Area
        options:
          - { value: money, label: Money }
          - { value: safety, label: Safety }
          - { value: other, label: Something else }
      - { type: textarea, name: message, label: What happened?, required: true, rows: 6, maxLength: 10000 }
      - type: pgpKey
        name: key
        label: Public key for a reply
        hint: Only if you want a reply. A key that carries your name tells us who you are.
Why like this

anonymous: true takes away the page, the reply address and the captcha
(6.1).
mode: required: the tip leaves the browser only encrypted. Without JavaScript the form cannot
send; it says so itself.
A key instead of an address for the reply. Whoever gives an anonymous public key (one without a
real name, made for this purpose) can receive an encrypted reply, as text on a page for instance,
without naming an address.
maxLength: 10000 on the text area keeps the encrypted submission below maxBytes. Without
the limit, the build says that a very long message would be refused.

What still holds
The host’s access log and the visitor’s network are beyond what a form can promise. Whoever really
has to protect a whistleblower says so on the page and names ways such as the Tor Browser.

en/forms/8-recipes/06-without-your-own-s.title: 8.6 – Without your own server
en/forms/8-recipes/06-without-your-own-s.content:
A website on GitHub Pages, Netlify or another host without PHP cannot run a relay. A form works all
the same, through a service.
Formspree
Create a form at Formspree; its id is in its address (formspree.io/f/xyzabcde):
options:
  transport:
    kind: formspree
    url: xyzabcde
  forms:
    contact:
      template: contact
The recipient address is set at Formspree, not here.
Web3Forms
Get an access key from Web3Forms:
options:
  transport:
    kind: web3forms
    url: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
The key is in the website’s HTML. Anyone can read it and use it to send to the address stored at
Web3Forms, and to no other.
An endpoint of your own
For any other service, or a script of your own that takes a POST:
options:
  transport:
    kind: endpoint
    url: forms.example.org/submit
    format: json
    extra:
      site: handbook
How the fields arrive and what the endpoint should answer is in
5.1.
The mail program
forms:
  contact:
    template: contact
    recipient: me@example.org
    transport:
      kind: mailto
On sending, the visitor’s mail program opens with subject and text; it is sent from there. The
address is in the website’s HTML.
What is missing, what remains

































With a serviceChecking in the browseras alwaysEncryptionas always; the service gets the ciphertext in the field message and does not see the contentHoneypot, time trap in the browseryesTime trap on the server, proof of work, rate limitno; the build says so when they are setCaptchayes, the service checks it itselfAnonymousonly in part: the service sees every sender’s address, and the build warns about it

en/forms/8-recipes/index.content:

en/forms/9-reference/03-limits.title: 9.3 – Limits
en/forms/9-reference/03-limits.content:
No file attachments
A form takes text, numbers, choices and a pasted public key, but no files. An attachment would have
to be encrypted, limited and put together by the relay as a mail attachment; that does not exist.
A submission is a mail
There is no database and no analysis. Whoever wants to count survey answers counts mails
(8.4).
The relay needs PHP
send.php runs on classic web hosting with PHP 8.1 or later and mbstring. For hosts without PHP the
services, an endpoint of your own or mailto remain (8.6),
with less protection.
Not measured yet
The plugin is measured on built websites in Chrome, the relay with a test suite under php -S. Not
measured yet are:

real mail delivery through mail() or sendmail,
the relay under Apache, nginx and PHP-FPM on a real host, and an upload over SFTP or FTP,
Firefox, Safari and phones; the proof of work on a phone,
a captcha widget after a page change in a real browser.

German and English only
quartz-forms’ sentences exist in these two languages; any other gets English until texts supplies
its wording (7.1). The page the relay answers a plain post
without JavaScript with cannot be changed and uses the informal “du” in German.
Fixed words in the message
The lines Page: … and Public key of the sender: follow the page’s language and can be changed
through texts (messagePage, messageKey). A mail the relay writes itself always has the
plugin’s own sentences, though: that is every unencrypted message through the relay, with or
without JavaScript.
Patterns: JavaScript and PCRE
Browser and relay read pattern with two different engines. The build refuses what only JavaScript
knows, and generating the relay configuration checks against your own machine’s PHP. What the host’s
PCRE still cannot read makes the relay refuse every value of the field
(2.2).
What encryption and anonymity do not achieve
Scripts on the same page see what is typed; the host’s access log and the visitor’s network are
outside the plugin (6.2, 6.1).
The rate limit is a quota for everyone
It counts without addresses and can therefore be used up by a single client for an hour
(6.3).
Container queries
Field widths need Chrome 105, Safari 16 or Firefox 110. An older browser shows every field across
the whole row.
