en/navigations/6-mobile/01-the-five-mode.title: 6.1 – The five modes
en/navigations/6-mobile/01-the-five-mode.content:
options:
  variant: dropdown
  mobile: offcanvas   # same (default) | accordion | offcanvas | select | hidden





























mobileBelow the mobile breakpointsamestays as it is; a row wrapsaccordionbecomes a stacked list with expandable foldersoffcanvasdisappears behind a burger button and slides in as a panel from the leftselectbecomes a jump menuhiddendisappears
same
For everything that is narrow anyway: tree, accordion, pager, select. For a horizontal bar
only if it has very few entries.
accordion
A row becomes a list stacked vertically, and folders with children become expandable. On smartphones they
start closed — except the path to the current page and whatever persistState remembered. On the
desktop they stay open and their title a link; the expand button is invisible there.
Suits bar, tabs and columns, which otherwise have no expandable folders, and dropdown and
mega, whose menus move into the flow of the page on smartphones.
If someone rotates their tablet across the breakpoint, the folders follow — they close or open without
reloading the page.
offcanvas
options:
  variant: bar
  depth: 2
  mobile: offcanvas
layout:
  position: header
In place of the navigation there is a burger button. It opens a panel that slides in from the
left, with a close button at the top and a dimmed background behind it. The panel shows the navigation
as a stacked list with expandable folders, as with accordion.
The panel closes via the button, a click on the background, Escape or a page change. While it is
open, the page behind it does not scroll.
That is the usual choice for the menu bar in the header.


                  
                  Not in a column that holds its children 
                  
                

The panel sits fixed over the window (position: fixed). An ancestor with transform, filter or a
mask turns “over the window” into “over this ancestor” — the panel then appears squashed or cut off.
The header of a Quartz site is the safe place for it; a scrolling sidebar is not.


It can be operated by keyboard too: the switch behind the burger button is a checkbox that receives
focus and reports its state through aria-expanded.
select
The list gives way to a jump menu, as variant: select shows (4.3):
first-level folders as groups, folder pages as “Overview”. It does not get more compact — but you only
see the structure once you open the menu. Needs JavaScript.
Suits a large sidebar that would end up below the text on a smartphone.
hidden
The navigation disappears. Right when another navigation takes over its job on smartphones — a sidebar with
hidden next to a header bar with offcanvas, for instance. The chapter navigation of this website is
hidden; on smartphones the pager below the text remains.
Quartz’s own display
Quartz knows display: desktop-only and mobile-only in the layout block. It works similarly to
mobile: hidden but is applied by Quartz itself: the component is then wrapped in a container of its
own, and the breakpoint is Quartz’s. mobile: hidden hides the navigation itself and can honour a
different breakpoint from breakpoints (6.2).

en/navigations/6-mobile/02-breakpoints.title: 6.2 – Breakpoints
en/navigations/6-mobile/02-breakpoints.content:
Where the breakpoint comes from
Quartz 5 has no option for its breakpoints in quartz.config.yaml. They are in the project’s
quartz/styles/variables.scss:
$breakpoints: (
  mobile: 800px,
  desktop: 1200px,
);
The plugin reads this file when the build creates the navigation and puts the value into its
stylesheet and script. Move the site’s breakpoint, and you move it for all navigations too — without a
second place you could forget.
If the file cannot be read, the plugin uses Quartz’s defaults, 800 and 1200 pixels, and says so once
(9.2).
Mobile means: at most this wide. With mobile: 800px a window of exactly 800 pixels is already
mobile, one of 801 is not.


                  
                  Restart after a change 
                  
                

The file is read when the navigation is created, not for every page. After changing
variables.scss, restart npx quartz build --serve.


Overriding
options:
  breakpoints:
    mobile: 640px
Pixels, rem and em are allowed; a bare number counts as pixels. desktop is accepted but currently
used by no rule of the plugin.


                  
                  The same in every entry — or not at all 
                  
                

The plugin’s stylesheet applies to all navigations of a site, not to a single one. If only one
entry sets a different breakpoint, the stylesheet ends up on the site twice, once with each
breakpoint, and both apply to every navigation. Between the two values every navigation then looks
half mobile. If you need a different breakpoint, change it in variables.scss — or set
breakpoints to the same value in every entry.


How this fits the layout
Quartz’s own layout wraps at the same breakpoint, because it reads the same file. A navigation with
mobile: offcanvas therefore turns into a burger button exactly when the sidebars slide below the
text.
With layout frames from QuartzControl that is not the
case. A frame brings its own breakpoints, stored in the project’s .quartz-gui/layout-breakpoints.json,
and does not read variables.scss. This website is such a case: its frame goes mobile below 900
pixels, variables.scss says 800. Both entries therefore carry
options:
  breakpoints:
    mobile: 900px
— the same value in every entry, so the stylesheet lands on the site only once.

en/navigations/6-mobile/index.title: 6 – Mobile
en/navigations/6-mobile/index.content:
A menu bar with six entries fits on a monitor, not on a smartphone. Every navigation therefore decides on
its own what becomes of it below the mobile breakpoint.

















PageContent6.1 – The five modessame, accordion, offcanvas, select, hidden6.2 – BreakpointsWhere the breakpoint comes from, and how to move it

en/navigations/7-appearance/01-icons.title: 7.1 – Icons
en/navigations/7-appearance/01-icons.content:
The glyphs
Rows carry a symbol before the title, like a file explorer:

























SymbolForfoldera folderopen foldera folder that is open — or, where nothing expands, that contains the current pagepagea page, also “Overview”housethe “Home” entry from showHome
Where they appear depends on the variant:





















VariantGlyphstree, accordion, flyouton every leveldropdown, mega, columnsin the menus and columns, not in the top rowbar, tabs, select, pagernone
Custom icons
A custom icon replaces the glyph of its row — and also appears in variants that otherwise show no
glyphs, in bar, tabs and the pager. Only not in select: an option of a select menu cannot hold
an image.
In the page’s frontmatter:
---
title: Guides
navIcon: lucide:book-open
---
In an index.md it applies to the folder.
In the configuration, by path — for folders without index.md, or when all icons should be in one
place:
options:
  nodeIcons:
    docs: lucide:book-open
    docs/api: "🧩"
    blog: none
If both places say something, the frontmatter wins.
What an icon can be

























ValueResultlucide:book-openthe Lucide icon as an embedded SVG📘the emoji§a short textnoneno symbol at all, not even a glyph
Lucide is a free icon set with well over a thousand symbols; the names are on
lucide.dev/icons. The whole set is inside the plugin — nothing to install
in the site. An unknown name prints a message at build time and shows nothing.
Icons are slightly larger than the text (1.1em), in the navigation’s muted colour, and in the accent
colour on the current page and its path.
icons — what is shown
options:
  icons: both   # both (default) | type | custom | none






























ValueGlyphsCustom iconsbothwhere no custom icon is setyestypeyesnocustomnoyesnonenono
true and false are understood as both and none.
iconNames — the plugin’s own symbols
The glyphs, the chevron, the burger button and the pager arrows are Lucide icons too. Each can be
swapped, with the name without lucide::
options:
  iconNames:
    folder: folder-closed
    chevron: chevron-right
    next: arrow-right
    previous: arrow-left


















































KeyDefaultWherefolderfolderfolderfolderOpenfolder-openopen folderfilefilepagehomehouse”Home”chevronchevron-downchevron on expandable foldersmenumenuburger buttonclosexclose in the mobile menuprevious, nextchevron-left, chevron-rightpager


                  
                  A right-pointing chevron turns differently 
                  
                

An open folder rotates its chevron by 180 degrees — right for chevron-down. With chevron-right
you want 90 degrees: .quartz-nav { --quartz-nav-chevron-open-rotate: 90deg; }
(7.2).

en/navigations/7-appearance/02-css-varia.title: 7.2 – CSS variables
en/navigations/7-appearance/02-css-varia.content:
Where to set them
In the project’s quartz/styles/custom.scss:
.quartz-nav {
  --quartz-nav-indent: 1.5rem;
  --quartz-nav-color-active: var(--tertiary);
}
That wins without higher specificity: Quartz puts every component’s CSS into a CSS layer
(@layer quartz-base), custom.scss not — and rules outside a layer beat rules inside one.
A single navigation
Every navigation carries its ID in the data-quartz-nav attribute:
.quartz-nav[data-quartz-nav="sidebar"] {
  --quartz-nav-bg-hover: transparent;
}
The ID is the value of id — without id, a checksum that changes with every option. So give a
navigation you style specifically an id (7.3).
Alternatively className adds classes of your own to the <nav>.
Colours and fonts
The defaults refer to Quartz’s theme variables and therefore follow dark mode.




































































































VariableDefaultEffect--quartz-nav-color--darkgraylinks--quartz-nav-color-hover--secondarylinks on hover--quartz-nav-color-active--secondarythe current page--quartz-nav-color-trail--secondaryfolders on the path to the current page--quartz-nav-color-static--darkfolder titles without a link--quartz-nav-color-heading--darkthe title heading--quartz-nav-color-muted--graychevrons, labels--quartz-nav-color-icon--grayglyphs and icons--quartz-nav-bg-hover--highlightbackground on hover--quartz-nav-bg-active--highlightbackground of the current page--quartz-nav-bg-panel--lightmenus, panels, mobile menu--quartz-nav-border--lightgrayborders and guide lines--quartz-nav-focus--secondaryfocus ring--quartz-nav-shadowsoft shadow, stronger in dark modemenus and panels--quartz-nav-backdroprgba(0,0,0,.35), .55 in dark modebackground behind the mobile menu--quartz-nav-font--bodyFontfont of the entries--quartz-nav-heading-font--headerFontfont of the heading--quartz-nav-folder-font--quartz-nav-heading-fontfont of folder titles
Spacing and shape






































































VariableDefaultEffect--quartz-nav-gap0.25rem 0.5remgap in horizontal rows--quartz-nav-nested-gap0.25rem 0.5remgap of the sublevels in bar--quartz-nav-indent1remindentation per level--quartz-nav-item-padding-y, -x0.2rem, 0.5rempadding of a row--quartz-nav-radius4pxcorner radius of a row--quartz-nav-line-height1.6line height--quartz-nav-row-heightline height plus paddingheight of the expand button--quartz-nav-toggle-size1.75remwidth of the expand button--quartz-nav-icon-size1.1emsize of the icons--quartz-nav-accent-bar3pxaccent bar on the current page--quartz-nav-chevron-open-rotate180degrotation of the chevron on an open folder--quartz-nav-title-size, --quartz-nav-title-margin1rem, 0 0 0.5remthe title heading
Menus, columns, mobile menu




























































VariableDefaultEffect--quartz-nav-panel-min-width12remminimum width of a menu--quartz-nav-panel-padding0.5rempadding of a menu--quartz-nav-panel-radius6pxcorner radius of a menu--quartz-nav-panel-z20stacking order of menus--quartz-nav-mega-min-widthmin(40rem, 90vw)width of the mega menu--quartz-nav-column-min-width10remminimum column width in columns and mega--quartz-nav-column-gap1rem 1.5remgap between columns--quartz-nav-offcanvas-widthmin(20rem, 85vw)width of the mobile menu--quartz-nav-offcanvas-padding1rempadding of the mobile menu--quartz-nav-offcanvas-z100stacking order of the mobile menu
Type by level
Folder rows get smaller and lighter with each level: level 1 is a section, level 2 a chapter,
everything below a place. Pages stay light and at most as large as --quartz-nav-page-size. The top
row of the horizontal variants, by contrast, is uniform.





































VariableDefault--quartz-nav-level-1-size, -weight0.95rem, 700--quartz-nav-level-2-size, -weight0.9rem, 600--quartz-nav-level-3-size, -weight0.875rem, 500--quartz-nav-level-4-size, -weight0.8rem, 500 — for level 4 and deeper--quartz-nav-page-size, --quartz-nav-page-weight0.875rem, 400--quartz-nav-bar-weight500 — top row of bar, dropdown, mega, tabs--quartz-nav-weight-active600 — the current page
Motion
Chevrons rotate, colours fade, folders and menus fade in when opening, the mobile menu slides in.
Everything hangs on one variable:
.quartz-nav {
  --quartz-nav-transition: 0s;   /* default: 0.2s ease */
}
With prefers-reduced-motion the plugin sets it to 0s itself.

en/navigations/7-appearance/03-markup-an.title: 7.3 – Markup and accessibility
en/navigations/7-appearance/03-markup-an.content:
The structure
nav.quartz-nav.quartz-nav--<variant>.quartz-nav--mobile-<mode>
  h3.quartz-nav__title                                  title
  div.quartz-nav__panel
    div.quartz-nav__root > a.quartz-nav__root-link       showScopeRoot
    ul.quartz-nav__list[data-level]
      li.quartz-nav__item.quartz-nav__item--page|--folder
        a.quartz-nav__link > icon + span.quartz-nav__text
        details.quartz-nav__folder > summary + ul        expandable folders

Depending on variant and mode there are also: button, background and close button of the mobile menu,
the jump menu, the two links of the pager. All classes carry the quartz-nav prefix; the explorer and
other components are not touched.
States

































Class / attributeWhereactive<li> and <a> of the current pagearia-current="page"link of the current pageactive-trailevery folder on the path to itquartz-nav__item--parentfolders whose children are shownquartz-nav__item--splitrows with a link and their own expand buttonquartz-nav--align-<value>horizontal variants
id
options:
  id: sidebar
Every navigation has an ID. Without id the plugin derives it from all options (nav- and a
checksum). You need a fixed id in three cases:

CSS for exactly this navigation — .quartz-nav[data-quartz-nav="sidebar"]. A checksum changes
with every option, and the selector would miss.
persistState — memory is stored under the ID. With a checksum it is gone after every option
change (5.1).
Two navigations with identical options on one page. They would have the same ID and therefore
the same element IDs — the burger button of one would open the menu of the other.

Letters, digits, - and _ are allowed; anything else becomes -.
Keyboard and screen reader

Every navigation is a <nav> with a name of its own: ariaLabel, otherwise title, otherwise
“Main navigation” — for the pager “Previous and next page”. With several navigations on one page,
each deserves its own ariaLabel or a title, so they can be told apart in the list of landmarks.
Expandable folders are <details> and <summary>. With folderClick: toggle the row is a
single control with the title; with link the title is a link and the button next to it is called
“Expand ”. No link sits inside a button.
Chevrons and icons are hidden from screen readers.
Menus close with Escape and return focus to their folder; trigger: hover also opens on keyboard
focus (5.2).
The mobile menu hangs on a focusable checkbox with aria-expanded and aria-controls; Escape
closes it and puts focus back.
The jump menu navigates by keyboard only on Enter, not while arrowing through.
Motion is dropped with prefers-reduced-motion.

The plugin’s words
“Main navigation”, “Overview”, “Home”, “Previous”, “Next”, “Jump to…”, “Go” and “Expand …” come with
the plugin in English and German. Which language it uses is decided on a multilingual site by the
language of the page (8.3), otherwise by the site’s locale:
German for de-DE and any other German variant such as de-AT, English for everything else.
title and ariaLabel can be changed; the others cannot. The plugin does not translate these two: on
a bilingual site a navigation with its own text therefore needs one entry per language. What that
looks like is in 8.3.

en/navigations/7-appearance/index.title: 7 – Appearance
en/navigations/7-appearance/index.content:
The plugin ships one stylesheet that follows the Quartz theme: the same colours, the same fonts, the
same dark mode. Without a single line of your own CSS a navigation already fits the site. Whatever can
be changed is a CSS variable.





















PageContent7.1 – IconsFolder and page symbols, custom icons, Lucide7.2 – CSS variablesEvery setting, and how to target a single navigation7.3 – Markup and accessibilityClasses, states, IDs and what a screen reader hears

en/navigations/8-recipes/01-the-navigati.title: 8.1 – The navigations of this site
en/navigations/8-recipes/01-the-navigati.content:
Two navigations are visible on this page: the menu in the left column, with the chapter of the
current page expanded, and the previous/next links below the text. On smartphones the menu becomes a
drawer behind a burger button. In the configuration they are two entries, and both serve both
languages.























idVariantPlaceLanguagemenueaccordionleft column, a drawer on smartphonesthe page’sseiten-pagerpagerbelow the textthe page’s
It is the same navigation as in the template this website is built with, with one difference: both
entries show only the handbook the page belongs to. On the right is Quartz’s own table of contents for the page.
How the languages are laid out here
The German pages are in one folder per plugin (navigations/), the English ones under en/
(en/navigations/);
quartz-multilanguage recognises English by the
folder and gives every other page the default language, German. From that the navigation builds one
tree per language: the German one holds only the German pages, the English one only the English
pages, and without the folder en — en/navigations/1-getting-started appears in it as
navigations/1-getting-started. How
this works for every layout is in 8.3.
The menu
  - source: "@quartz-community/explorer"
    enabled: false
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: accordion
      scope: section
      showHome: true
      folderClick: toggle
      indexEntry: first
      exclusive: true
      mobile: offcanvas
      id: menue
      className: nav-menue
      breakpoints:
        mobile: 900px
        desktop: 1200px
    layout:
      position: left
      priority: 30

Instead of the explorer. Quartz’s explorer is switched off; the menu stands in its place.
One entry for both languages. Without a title there is no text of its own, and with the
default language: auto the menu shows the nine German chapters on German pages and the nine
English ones on English pages.
scope: section shows only the first-level folder the page lies in: the handbook of one of
the four plugins. The start page has no section, so the menu stays away there
(3.1).
accordion with every page. The chapter of the current page is open, the page marked
(5.1).
exclusive keeps one chapter open at a time; nine open chapters would be 45 rows.
folderClick: toggle: a click anywhere on a chapter row expands and collapses it.
indexEntry: first therefore puts “Overview” as the first row into every chapter — otherwise
the chapter page could not be reached from the menu
(3.2).
showHome puts “Home” in front, “Start” on German pages — each time the start page of the
page’s own language.
mobile: offcanvas puts the menu behind a burger button on smartphones
(6.1).
className: nav-menue is the name under which the template styles the menu: the drawer, the
burger where the explorer’s button would otherwise sit, colours and spacing from its variables.
This website needs no file of its own for it.

The pager
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: pager
      scope: section
      id: seiten-pager
      className: nav-pager
      breakpoints:
        mobile: 900px
        desktop: 1200px
    layout:
      position: afterBody
      priority: 80
One entry for both languages. With the default language: auto the pager pages through the tree
of the language the page is written in: after the last German page nothing follows, not the English
start page. And with scope: section it stays in the handbook: after the last page about
quartz-navigations comes not the first one about another plugin.
The words come out right by themselves. “Previous” and “Next” on English pages, “Zurück” and
“Weiter” on German ones, and the name for screen readers likewise
(7.3). Neither labels: false nor an ariaLabel is
needed.
What both entries share

breakpoints in both entries, because this website’s layout frame breaks at 900 pixels and
not at the 800 from variables.scss (6.2). desktop is accepted
but currently used by no rule of the plugin.
The same tree-shaping options. The build therefore computes two trees, one per language, and
not four (1.3).

What is not switched on here
stripNumericPrefix. The titles of this website start with their number — “8.1 – The navigations …” —
and the option would take “8.” off (2.1). Sorting is
still right: by the numbers of the file and folder names, 01-…, 02-….

en/navigations/8-recipes/02-a-docs-site.title: 8.2 – A docs site
en/navigations/8-recipes/02-a-docs-site.content:
Documentation with a few sections, each with some chapters:
index.md
getting-started/ index.md, installation.md, first-steps.md
guides/          index.md, import/…, export/…
reference/       index.md, cli.md, configuration.md

The four entries
plugins:
  # 1 · Header: the sections, their pages in the menu, behind the burger button on smartphones
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: dropdown
      depth: 2
      trigger: hover
      folderClick: link
      mobile: offcanvas
      ariaLabel: Sections
      id: header
    layout:
      position: header
      priority: 20
 
  # 2 · Sidebar: only the section you are reading
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: accordion
      scope: section
      showScopeRoot: true
      persistState: true
      mobile: hidden
      ariaLabel: This section
      id: section
    layout:
      position: left
      priority: 20
 
  # 3 · Below the text: paging, but not beyond the section
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: pager
      scope: section
      id: pager
    layout:
      position: afterBody
      priority: 10
 
  # 4 · Footer: the whole site in columns
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: columns
      depth: 2
      mobile: accordion
      ariaLabel: Sitemap
      id: sitemap
    layout:
      position: footer
      priority: 10
Why like this
Every navigation has one job. The header says which sections exist. The column says where you are
within a section. The pager says what comes next. The footer is where you look when you are lost.
Header: depth: 2 keeps the menu flat — sections and what they contain. Subfolders such as
import appear as a row linking to their folder page, their pages do not. hover with link
opens on hover and leads to the section page on click (5.2). On
smartphones the whole bar becomes a burger menu.
Column: scope: section shows only guides while you read the guides. The start page has no
section; the column stays empty there, and that is right — the header shows all sections.
mobile: hidden, because the burger menu does the same job on smartphones.
Pager: with scope: section, paging ends at the last chapter of the section instead of silently
jumping into the next one.
Footer: mobile: accordion collapses the columns into a list on smartphones whose sections can be
opened.
ariaLabel everywhere except on the pager, because three of the four <nav> would otherwise be
called “Main navigation”; the pager is called “Previous and next page” on its own
(7.3).
And the explorer?
Switch it off — enabled: false on the @quartz-community/explorer entry. The column takes over its
job for the current section, the header for the rest.
Variations

























If …then …the sections have many subfoldersheader as mega with depth: 3there are only three or four sections and you should see which one you are inheader as tabs, no menu thenthe order of the sections should not be alphabeticalorder: { "": [getting-started, guides, reference] } in all entries, or navOrder in the index.md filesthe pager should lead through the whole documentationleave out scope on the pager

en/navigations/8-recipes/03-more-recipes.title: 8.3 – More recipes
en/navigations/8-recipes/03-more-recipes.content:
Replacing the explorer
  - source: "@quartz-community/explorer"
    enabled: false
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: accordion
      folderClick: link
      persistState: true
      stripNumericPrefix: true
      mobile: offcanvas
      id: explorer
    layout:
      position: left
      priority: 30
Like the explorer, but with folder rows that lead to their page, an order of your own
(2.2) and a burger menu on smartphones. The fixed id keeps the memory across
later option changes.
stripNumericPrefix only if the titles do not start with a number themselves
(2.1).
A blog by date
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: pager
      rootPath: blog
      sort: date
      sortDirection: desc
      ariaLabel: Newer and older post
      id: blog-pager
    layout:
      position: afterBody
      priority: 10
Visible only below blog, newest first. Note: with desc, “Previous” is the newer post and “Next”
the older — the order of the list, not of time. Posts without a date come last. A sidebar in manual
order gets along with it (1.3).
Multilingual sites
With quartz-multilanguage, one entry shows the
tree of each page’s language on every page, with no further option:
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: accordion
      id: navigation
    layout:
      position: left
      priority: 30
That holds for all four layouts quartz-multilanguage knows:

























LayoutExampleLanguage foldersde/docs/setup.md, en/docs/setup.mdDefault language in the rootdocs/setup.md, en/docs/setup.mdLanguage suffix in the file namedocs/Setup.md, docs/Setup.en.mdLanguage in the frontmatterblog/hallo.md with lang: de, blog/hello.md with lang: en
quartz-multilanguage stores on every page its language and a path without language folder or suffix:
en/docs/setup and docs/setup.en both become docs/setup. The navigation places pages by that path
but links to the real ones. Generated folder pages, which carry no language, get into the right
language through the pages next to them.

Paths in the options are language-neutral. rootPath: docs, order, nodeIcons and
include/exclude apply to every language alike. include and exclude also match the real path,
so exclude: [en] leaves out the English pages.
The plugin’s words and alphabetical sorting follow the page
(7.3, 2.2).
Your own texts do not. title and ariaLabel read the same in every language. If you need a
heading, add one entry per language with a fixed language
(below).
A language folder’s start page (de/index.md) wins over an index.md in the root.

The option language





















ValueEffectauto (default)the tree in the language of the current pagea language code such as de or en-USalways that language’s tree; en-US finds pages marked enallno languages: one tree with every page, language folders as folders — the behaviour up to version 0.2
A code no page carries yields no navigation and a message (9.2). Pages
that belong to several languages or to none — a folder page shared by suffix pages, tag pages — get
the default language, the way quartz-multilanguage decides for them (9.3).
A heading per language
A chapter tree in the right column, headed “In diesem Kapitel” on German pages and “In this chapter”
on English ones:
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: tree
      language: de
      scope: section
      showScopeRoot: true
      title: In diesem Kapitel
      mobile: hidden
      id: kapitel-de
    layout:
      position: right
      priority: 5
The English entry differs in language: en, in title and id.

Two entries, because title is text. The navigation translates the plugin’s own words, not a
heading of yours.
language: de always shows the German tree. On an English page the page is not in it,
scope: section finds no chapter, and the entry does not appear
(3.1). The English one disappears on German pages in the
same way — so every page shows exactly one.
scope: section shows the chapter the page is in; showScopeRoot puts the chapter name
above it as a link.

Until 24 September 2026 exactly this tree stood on this website. It gave way to the template’s
menu, which expands the current page’s chapter by itself
(8.1).
Entries per language folder from version 0.2
Up to version 0.2 every language needed its own entry, with rootPath: en or exclude: [en]. Such
entries keep working: a rootPath that names a language folder shows that language’s tree from the
folder on, and with hideOutsideRoot only on pages inside it. include: [en] has the same effect. The
separate entries are only needed for your own texts now.
Sections as tabs above the text
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: tabs
      align: full
      mobile: select
      ariaLabel: Sections
      id: tabs
    layout:
      position: beforeBody
      priority: 5
The sections as tabs across the full width, the pages of the active section in the second row. On
smartphones a jump menu instead of two rows that wrap.
A jump menu on smartphones only
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: tree
      depth: 2
      mobile: select
      title: Contents
      id: contents
    layout:
      position: left
      priority: 30
On the desktop a tree in the column, on smartphones a single select field that takes hardly any room. The
title sits above in both versions.
A sitemap for part of the site only
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: columns
      rootPath: docs
      hideOutsideRoot: false
      depth: 2
      title: Documentation
      id: docs-sitemap
    layout:
      position: footer
      priority: 10
hideOutsideRoot: false shows the documentation in the footer on every page of the site, not only
inside docs (3.2).

en/navigations/9-reference/02-messages.title: 9.2 – Messages
en/navigations/9-reference/02-messages.content:
All messages start with [navigations] and appear once per cause, not once per page. None of them
stops the build: the plugin takes the default or leaves out what is broken and keeps building.
Unknown value "…" for `…`; using `…`.
A value the option does not know — a typo, a German spelling (variant: baum), a value from another
option. The named default applies. The allowed values are in 9.1.
`…` must be an integer >= …; using ….
depth or columns.max is not an integer, or too small. depth: "2" in quotes works; depth: 1.5 and
depth: -1 do not.
Ignoring invalid `…` entry …
An entry in include, exclude or an order list is not text or is empty. Only that entry is dropped.
`order` must be a map of folder → list. · `nodeIcons` must be a map of path → icon.
The option is a list instead of a map. Correct:
order:
  docs: [intro, setup]
nodeIcons:
  docs: lucide:book-open
Ignoring invalid `nodeIcons` entry for "…".
The value for this path is empty or not text.
`order` for "…" lists unknown entry "…".
A folder’s order list names something that does not exist in it — usually a renamed file, or a slug
instead of a file name with different spelling. The other entries still apply. See
2.2.
`rootPath: …` is not a folder with visible pages.
The folder does not exist, rootPath names a page instead of a folder, or everything in it is hidden —
by exclude, navHide, drafts. The navigation appears on no page.
`language: …` matches no page language (…).
The fixed language matches none of the languages quartz-multilanguage recorded on the pages; the
parentheses list the ones that exist. Usually a typo, or a language that has no page yet. The navigation
appears on no page (8.3).
Unknown Lucide icon `…`; see lucide.dev/icons
A name from navIcon, nodeIcons or iconNames is not in the Lucide set. No icon appears there.
Common causes: a name from an older Lucide version (home is house today), or with iconNames a
superfluous lucide: in front.
Could not read quartz/styles/variables.scss; using 800px / 1200px as breakpoints.
The build is not running in the project folder, or the file is missing. The navigation switches to
mobile at 800 pixels (6.2).
`variant: vertical` is now `tree`. · `dropdownTrigger` is now `trigger`.
Old spellings from version 0.1. They still work; the message goes away as soon as the new spelling is
used.
`style` was removed; …
The style option no longer exists and is skipped. Styling is done through the CSS variables
(7.2).
When nothing happens at all
No message, no navigation — then it is rarely the plugin:

























CauseWhat helpsenabled: falseswitch itThe scope is empty on this pagecheck scope, rootPath, hideOutsideRoot (3.1)The pager has no neighboursthe page is hidden, or it is the only one in the scopeThe navigation sits in an unexpected placelayout block missing — then left, priority: 10

en/navigations/9-reference/03-limits.title: 9.3 – Limits
en/navigations/9-reference/03-limits.content:
Only pages from the content folder
A menu item that leads to another website is not a page and appears in no tree. Quartz’s footer
(links) or a layout box is there for that.
The words exist only in German and English
“Previous”, “Next”, “Overview”, “Home” and the names for screen readers come with the plugin in these
two languages; every other language gets English. Only title and ariaLabel can be changed, and the
plugin does not translate them (7.3).
Shared pages get the default language
Tag pages and folder pages shared by several languages belong to no language. There the navigation
shows the tree of quartz-multilanguage’s default language — even on the tag page of an English tag. If
every page lives in a language folder, the site’s locale decides instead
(8.3).
With the language in the frontmatter, only one language has a start page
The index.md in the root belongs to exactly one language. The other language’s tree has no start
page: showHome and showScopeRoot with scope: root show nothing there.
detection with frontmatter before folder
If you reorder detection in quartz-multilanguage that way, pages in a language folder that carry lang
in the frontmatter keep the folder in their path; the others lose it. The English tree then shows
docs twice: in the root and under en. With the default [folder, suffix, frontmatter] this does
not happen.
breakpoints does not apply to a single navigation
The stylesheet is one for all. Different values in different entries end up as two stylesheets on the
site, both acting on every navigation (6.2).
stripNumericPrefix also hits titles from the frontmatter
Not only titles from file names but every title that starts with a number and -, _, . or a
space. “1.2 – Getting started” becomes “2 – Getting started”. Only navTitle stays untouched
(2.1).
columns.max has no effect
The option is accepted, but the grid follows the width only (4.3).
The jump menu needs JavaScript
select and mobile: select navigate through a script. Without JavaScript an option can be chosen,
but nothing happens (5.3).
No custom icons in the jump menu
An option of a <select> can only hold text (7.1).
One order per navigation, not per page
Sorting applies to an entry’s whole tree. A page cannot ask to sit somewhere else in one navigation than
in another — unless the two navigations sort differently.
Hover only with a mouse
trigger: hover works on devices that report hover. On touch devices the click opens.
The mobile menu needs a clear path
It sits over the window with position: fixed. Inside an ancestor with transform, filter or a mask
it gets squashed or cut off (6.1).
exclusive depends on the browser
One folder per level through the name attribute of <details> is supported by current browsers. Older
ones leave several folders open — the navigation still works.
Memory depends on the ID
persistState stores under the id. Without a fixed id, every option change changes the ID and what
was remembered is gone (5.1). It is stored in the visitor’s
browser; another browser, a private window or cleared site data start from scratch.
Folders are remembered under their real path. With language folders, de/docs and en/docs are two
folders, and memory starts afresh after switching language; with language suffixes both languages share
one folder and with it what was open.

en/navigations/index.title: Navigations
en/navigations/index.content:
Quartz ships one navigation: the explorer, a folder tree in the sidebar. That’s it.
quartz-navigations builds every other navigation a website needs from the same folder
structure — a menu bar in the header, an accordion for the current section, a sitemap in the
footer, “previous” and “next” below the text. One plugin, as many entries as you like, and each
one chooses which part of the tree it shows and in what form.
What it does


                  
                  From the folder structure 
                  
                

The tree is built from the content’s folders at build time. Titles come from a folder’s
index.md or its name, the order by hand, alphabetically or by date. →
2




                  
                  As often as you like, each with its own scope 
                  
                

One plugin, as many entries as the site needs. Each shows the whole site, one section, the
current folder or only the siblings — and as many levels as it should. →
3




                  
                  Ten variants 
                  
                

Tree, accordion and flyout for the sidebar; bar, dropdown, mega menu and tabs for the header;
columns for the footer; a jump menu, and previous/next below the text. →
4




                  
                  On smartphones 
                  
                

Every navigation decides for itself what becomes of it below the mobile breakpoint: it stays,
turns into an accordion, goes behind a burger button, becomes a jump menu or disappears. →
6




                  
                  Without JavaScript, and usable by everyone 
                  
                

The navigation is finished in the HTML; a small script adds remembered folders, menus that open
on hover and the scroll lock behind a mobile menu. Whole rows are click targets, aria-current
marks the page, and a screen reader hears the words in the page’s language. →
5, 7.3




                  
                  Looks like the rest of the site 
                  
                

Colours, fonts and dark mode come from the theme; every value is a --quartz-nav-* variable.
Folder and page glyphs like a file manager, your own icon per page from Lucide. →
7


With quartz-multilanguage one entry shows every
page the tree of its own language, however the languages are laid out in the content
(8.3).


                  
                  This website is its own proof 
                  
                

It is built with the plugin. The menu in the left column, which becomes a drawer on smartphones, and
the previous/next links below every text are two entries of the plugin.
8.1 shows them and explains every option.


The nine chapters













































ChapterThe question it answers1 – Getting startedWhy the plugin, and how does the first navigation come about?2 – The treeWhere do titles and order come from, and what is left out on purpose?3 – The scopeThe whole site, one section or just the current folder?4 – The ten variantsTree, bar, accordion, menu, columns, pager — which one for what?5 – InteractionWhat happens when a folder is clicked, and what on hover?6 – MobileWhat becomes of a menu bar on a smartphone?7 – AppearanceIcons, colours, spacing — and how to change them8 – RecipesFinished combinations, one of them on this page9 – ReferenceEvery option, every message, every limit
In one minute
npx quartz plugin add github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
Then one entry per navigation. This one puts the first folder level into the header as a bar:
plugins:
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-navigations
    enabled: true
    options:
      variant: bar
      depth: 1
      mobile: offcanvas
    layout:
      position: header
      priority: 20
The details are in 1.2 – Your first navigation.
Where else it is written down
The short version is the repository README. The
sister plugins quartz-layout-box and
quartz-multilanguage work together with this one;
all three belong to QuartzControl, but the app is not
required.
Licence

are under ISC, © Lucide Contributors.

forms/1-einstieg/01-wozu-dieses-plugin.title: 1.1 – Wozu dieses Plugin
forms/1-einstieg/01-wozu-dieses-plugin.content:
Quartz baut aus Notizen eine statische Website: HTML-Dateien, die ein Webserver ausliefert, ohne
etwas auszurechnen. Ein Formular braucht aber jemanden, der die Eingaben annimmt und weitergibt.
Die Website selbst kann das nicht.
Drei übliche Auswege





















WegWas dabei passiertEin Formular-Dienst (Formspree, Web3Forms …)Der Dienst nimmt die Eingaben an und mailt sie weiter. Er sieht alles, was der Besucher schreibt, und seine Adresse.Ein Mail-Link (mailto:)Das Mailprogramm des Besuchers öffnet sich. Wer keins eingerichtet hat, kommt nicht weiter.Ein eingebettetes FremdformularEin Rahmen von Google, Microsoft oder einem anderen Anbieter, mit dessen Aussehen und dessen Datenschutz.
Was quartz-forms anders macht

Die Formulare gehören zur Website. Sie werden beim Bauen aus der quartz.config.yaml
erzeugt, sehen aus wie der Rest der Seite und sprechen ihre Sprache.
Geprüft wird im Browser, beim Verlassen eines Felds und beim Senden, mit Sätzen statt
Fehlercodes. Dieselben Regeln prüft der Bau vorher und das Relay hinterher.
Verschlüsselt wird im Browser. Mit OpenPGP verlässt nur ein verschlüsselter Block die Seite.
Der Server, der ihn weitergibt, kann ihn nicht lesen.
Zugestellt wird über den eigenen Webspace. Das mitgelieferte Relay ist eine einzelne
PHP-Datei. Es kennt die Empfängeradressen, die Website nur einen Namen dafür.
Ein Formular kann anonym sein, und der Code hält das Versprechen: keine Pflichtangaben zur
Person, keine Antwortadresse, kein Protokoll.

Die Formular-Dienste und mailto: bleiben als Versandweg möglich, für eine Website ohne PHP
(5.1).
Was es nicht ist

Keine Datenbank. Eine Sendung wird eine Mail. Wer Antworten auswerten will, wertet Mails
aus.
Keine Dateianhänge. Ein Formular nimmt Text, Zahlen, Auswahlen und einen öffentlichen
PGP-Schlüssel an, aber keine Dateien.
Kein Server. Das Relay ist ein Skript für klassisches Webhosting mit PHP, kein Dienst, den
jemand betreibt.

Was man braucht

Eine Website mit Quartz 5.
Für das Relay einen Webspace mit PHP ab 8.1 und der Erweiterung mbstring; das haben fast
alle Hoster. Ohne PHP geht es über einen Formular-Dienst oder mailto:.
Für verschlüsselte Formulare einen öffentlichen PGP-Schlüssel, etwa aus gpg, Thunderbird
oder Mailvelope.

forms/1-einstieg/02-das-erste-formular.title: 1.2 – Das erste Formular
forms/1-einstieg/02-das-erste-formular.content:
Vier Schritte, und das Formular steht auf der Seite.
1. Plugin installieren
npx quartz plugin add github:boxi-os/quartz-forms
Der Befehl holt das Plugin und trägt es in die quartz.config.yaml ein, mit allen Optionen und
ihren Vorgabewerten. Die lange Liste darf man kürzen: Was nicht dasteht, nimmt das Plugin selbst
als Vorgabe.
In QuartzControl geht dasselbe über den Marktplatz.
2. Das Formular beschreiben
plugins:
  - source: github:boxi-os/quartz-forms
    enabled: true
    options:
      transport:
        kind: relay
        url: example.org/forms/send.php
      forms:
        first-form:
          title: Ein erstes Formular
          recipient: owner
          fields:
            - { type: text, name: name, label: Name, autocomplete: name }
            - { type: email, name: email, label: E-Mail, autocomplete: email }
            - { type: textarea, name: message, label: Nachricht, required: true }

forms hält alle Formulare der Website, jedes unter einer Kennung aus Kleinbuchstaben,
Ziffern und Bindestrichen. Mit ihr bindet eine Seite das Formular ein.
fields sind die Felder in ihrer Reihenfolge (2.1).
transport sagt, wohin eine Sendung geht. Hier ist es das Relay auf dem eigenen Webspace
(5.2); recipient ist der Name, den das Relay auf eine Adresse
abbildet.

Wer erst ausprobieren will, schreibt transport: { kind: demo }. Dann sendet das Formular nichts
und zeigt, was angekommen wäre, so wie hier im Handbuch.
3. Einbinden
Auf einer beliebigen Seite, als Codeblock mit der Kennung:
```quartz-form
first-form
```
Die anderen Wege (Platzhalter, Frontmatter, Layout) stehen in Kapitel 3.
4. Ansehen
npx quartz build --serve
So sieht das Ergebnis aus:

Ein leeres Senden zeigt die Prüfung im Browser. Mit einer Nachricht zeigt das Formular, was
gesendet worden wäre.
Wenn etwas nicht stimmt

























Was zu sehen istWoran es liegtDer Codeblock steht als Code auf der SeiteDas Plugin ist nicht eingetragen oder enabled: false, oder codeBlockLang ist geändert (3.1).Der Bau bricht ab: embeds the form "…", which options.forms does not haveDie Kennung im Codeblock steht nicht unter forms. Mit --serve erscheint stattdessen ein Hinweis auf der Seite.Der Bau bricht ab: [forms] 2 problem(s) in the quartz-forms optionsEine Beschreibung ist fehlerhaft; die Zeilen darunter nennen Pfad und Grund (9.2).Das Formular sagt „Die Nachricht konnte nicht gesendet werden.“Das Ziel ist nicht erreichbar oder lehnt ab. Lehnt das Relay ab, nennt die Konsole des Browsers den Code (5.3).

forms/1-einstieg/03-was-beim-bauen-passi.title: 1.3 – Was beim Bauen passiert
forms/1-einstieg/03-was-beim-bauen-passi.content:
quartz-forms ist ein Plugin aus vier Teilen. Jeder hat eine Aufgabe, und zusammen entsteht aus
einem Eintrag in der Config ein Formular, das im Browser arbeitet.
1. Die Optionen werden gelesen und geprüft
Quartz übergibt dem Plugin die Optionen aus der quartz.config.yaml. Das Plugin ergänzt die
Vorgaben, legt Vorlagen darunter (2.1) und prüft jedes Formular: Kennung,
Feldnamen, Optionen, Bedingungen, Schritte, Versandweg, Schlüssel.

Ein Problem hält den Bau an. Die Meldung nennt den Pfad in der Config, etwa
forms.contact.fields[2]: unknown field type "textfield".
Ein Hinweis steht im Protokoll, und der Bau läuft weiter. Er sagt, was nicht wirkt oder
anders wirkt als vermutlich gemeint.

Alle Meldungen stehen in 9.2.
2. Die Seiten bekommen ihre Formulare
Der Transformer sucht auf jeder Seite nach Codeblöcken, Platzhaltern und dem
Frontmatter-Schlüssel (Kapitel 3) und setzt an ihre Stelle das fertige
HTML-Formular: Felder, Beschriftungen, Hinweise und, unsichtbar, die Regeln als JSON für das
Skript im Browser. Die Komponente tut dasselbe für das Formular, das über das Layout auf jeder
Seite steht (3.4).
Welche Sprache ein Formular spricht, entscheidet die Seite (7.1).
3. Die Schlüssel werden geprüft und die Verschlüsselung kopiert
Der Emitter prüft jeden öffentlichen Schlüssel, an den ein Formular verschlüsselt: lesbar,
öffentlich, nicht widerrufen, nicht abgelaufen, verschlüsselungsfähig. Den Fingerabdruck schreibt er
ins Protokoll:
[forms] key "demo": 3EEC 26B0 22A0 0814 0EAF 4AD0 9FED 4B8B 67FD D91B (quartz-forms Demo …)

Verschlüsselt mindestens ein Formular, kopiert er OpenPGP.js nach
static/quartz-forms/openpgp/. Der Browser lädt es nur auf Seiten, die es brauchen.
4. Im Browser
Ein Skript übernimmt jedes Formular auf der Seite: Es zeigt nur die Felder, deren Bedingungen
gelten, und einen Schritt auf einmal (Kapitel 4), prüft beim Verlassen eines
Felds und beim Senden, stellt die Spam-Fallen (6.3), verschlüsselt und sendet.
Ohne JavaScript bleibt ein gewöhnliches HTML-Formular übrig (4.3).
Was nicht auf die Website kommt
Die Adressen der Empfänger. Sie stehen nur in der Konfiguration des Relays auf dem Webspace; die
Website schickt die Kennung des Formulars mit, und das Relay sucht die Adresse dazu heraus. Wie
diese Konfiguration aus der quartz.config.yaml entsteht, steht in
5.2.

forms/1-einstieg/index.title: 1 – Einstieg
forms/1-einstieg/index.content: SeiteInhalt1.1 – Wozu dieses PluginWas eine statische Website mit einem Formular anfangen kann1.2 – Das erste FormularInstallieren, beschreiben, einbinden, ansehen1.3 – Was beim Bauen passiertVom Eintrag in der Config zum Formular im Browser

forms/2-felder/01-feldtypen.title: 2.1 – Feldtypen
forms/2-felder/01-feldtypen.content:
Ein Formular ist eine Liste von Feldern unter fields. Jedes Feld hat einen type und einen
name, fast jedes ein label.

Was jedes Feld hat





































SchlüsselBedeutungtypeDer Feldtyp, siehe unten.nameEin Buchstabe, dann Buchstaben, Ziffern, _ oder -; eindeutig im Formular. Unter diesem Namen kommt der Wert an.labelDie Beschriftung, ein Text. Pflicht außer bei hidden und consent.requiredtrue macht das Feld zur Pflicht (2.2).hintEin Satz unter dem Feld.widthfull, half oder third (2.3).showIfZeigt das Feld nur unter einer Bedingung (4.1).
Ein Text ist entweder eine Zeichenkette oder eine Zuordnung von Sprache zu Zeichenkette:
label: { de: Nachricht, en: Message }. Die Sprache der Seite wählt
(7.1).
Einige Namen gehören der Sendung selbst und sind für Felder gesperrt: form, lang, page,
pageTitle, ts, pow, captcha, encrypted, ciphertext, fields,
cf-turnstile-response, h-captcha-response und alles, was mit _ beginnt.
Die Typen





















































































typeWas es istEigene SchlüsseltextEine Zeile Textplaceholder, autocomplete, pattern, maxLengthemailEine E-Mail-Adressewie texttelEine Telefonnummerwie texturlEine Webadresse mit http:// oder https://wie textnumberEine Zahl; ein Komma gilt als Dezimalzeichenmin, max, step, placeholderdateEin Datum aus dem Kalender des Browsersautocomplete (etwa bday); placeholder und maxLength nimmt es an, Chrome zeigt und prüft sie bei einem Datum aber nichttextareaMehrere Zeilenrows, placeholder, pattern, maxLengthselectEine Auswahl aus einer aufklappenden ListeoptionsradioEine Auswahl aus sichtbaren Optionenoptions, layoutcheckboxesMehrere Auswahlenoptions, layoutcheckboxEin einzelnes Häkchen; angehakt kommt yes an–scaleEine Stufe zwischen zwei Enden, höchstens 21 Stufenmin, max (ganze Zahlen), minLabel, maxLabelconsentEine Einwilligung, immer Pflichttext, link, linkLabelpgpKeyDer öffentliche PGP-Schlüssel des Besuchers, eingefügt oder als Dateihöchstens einer je FormularhiddenEin fester Wert, den der Besucher nicht siehtvalue
pageBreak ist kein Feld, sondern beginnt einen Schritt (4.2).
Optionen sind eine Liste aus Wert und Beschriftung:
- type: radio
  name: reply
  label: { de: Wie sollen wir antworten?, en: How should we reply? }
  options:
    - { value: email, label: { de: Per E-Mail, en: By e-mail } }
    - { value: phone, label: { de: Per Telefon, en: By phone } }
Angekommen ist der Wert, angezeigt die Beschriftung. In der Mail stehen die Beschriftungen,
damit niemand die Werte nachschlagen muss.
Ein paar Einzelheiten

autocomplete sagt dem Browser, was er vorschlagen darf (name, email, tel …). Das
Relay setzt die Antwortadresse der Mail (Reply-To) auf das erste ausgefüllte email-Feld. Gibt
es mehrere, etwa die eigene Adresse und die eines Freundes, bekommt das des Besuchers
autocomplete: email; dann zählen nur solche Felder.
consent braucht einen text. link hängt einen Verweis an, etwa auf die
Datenschutzerklärung, linkLabel beschriftet ihn.
pgpKey nimmt einen öffentlichen Schlüssel an. Beim Verlassen prüft der Browser ihn und nennt
seinen Fingerabdruck; einen privaten Schlüssel weist er ab. Wozu das gut ist, steht in
6.2.
hidden geht mit jeder Sendung mit, etwa um zwei Formulare mit denselben Feldern
auseinanderzuhalten.

Vorlagen
Vier Feldsätze liegen bei: contact, feedback, rsvp und survey.
forms:
  contact:
    template: contact
Eine Vorlage bringt Titel, Felder und Voreinstellungen mit. Alles, was das Formular selbst angibt,
liegt darüber; eigene fields ersetzen die Felder der Vorlage ganz. Was jede Vorlage enthält, zeigen
die Rezepte: Kontakt, Feedback,
Umfrage. rsvp ist eine Anmeldung mit Name, E-Mail, Termin, Personenzahl,
Anmerkung und Einwilligung.

forms/2-felder/02-pflichtfelder-und-prue.title: 2.2 – Pflichtfelder und Prüfregeln
forms/2-felder/02-pflichtfelder-und-prue.content:
Die Regeln eines Felds stehen einmal, in seiner Beschreibung. Angewendet werden sie dreimal: beim
Bau, im Browser und im Relay.

Die Regeln








































SchlüsselGilt fürWirkungrequired: truejedes FeldLeer wird nicht gesendet. consent ist immer Pflicht.maxLengthTextfelderHöchstzahl der Zeichen. Ohne Angabe gilt spam.maxFieldLength (2000) für eine Zeile und spam.maxTextareaLength (20 000) für ein Textfeld.min, maxnumber, scaleDie kleinste und die größte Zahl.patterntext, textarea, email, tel, urlEin regulärer Ausdruck, dem der ganze Wert entsprechen muss.Typemail, url, tel, number, dateEine E-Mail-Adresse, eine http(s)-Adresse, eine Telefonnummer aus Ziffern, Leerzeichen und +()./-, eine Zahl, ein Tag, den es gibt.Optionenselect, radio, checkboxesNur Werte, die in options stehen.
Leerraum am Anfang und am Ende zählt nicht. Ein Feld, das nur aus Leerzeichen besteht, ist leer.
Wann der Browser prüft

Beim Verlassen eines Felds, sobald etwas darin steht oder ein Pflichtfeld leer bleibt. Der
Satz steht unter dem Feld und verschwindet, sobald der Wert stimmt.
Beim Senden alle Felder, die zählen. Unter dem Button steht dann „Bitte prüfe 3 Felder.“, und
der Fokus springt in das erste.

Die Sätze sprechen die Sprache der Seite:





































FallSatzPflichtfeld leer„Dieses Feld ist ein Pflichtfeld.“Keine Option gewählt„Bitte wähle eine Option.“ / „Bitte wähle mindestens eine Option.“Einwilligung fehlt„Bitte stimme vor dem Senden zu.“Zu lang„Bitte verwende höchstens 200 Zeichen.“Zahl außerhalb„Bitte gib mindestens 1 ein.“ / „Bitte gib höchstens 8 ein.“Muster verfehlt„Bitte verwende das verlangte Format.“Falsches Format„Bitte gib eine gültige E-Mail-Adresse ein.“ und entsprechend für Webadresse, Telefonnummer, Zahl, Datum
Jeder dieser Sätze lässt sich ersetzen (7.1). Weil „Bitte
verwende das verlangte Format.“ nicht sagt, welches, gehört zu jedem pattern ein hint.
Muster
pattern ist ein regulärer Ausdruck in JavaScript-Schreibweise. Er muss auf den ganzen Wert
passen; ^ und $ dürfen dastehen, nötig sind sie nicht.
- type: text
  name: zip
  label: Postleitzahl
  pattern: "^[0-9]{5}$"
  hint: Fünf Ziffern.
Das Relay prüft dasselbe Muster mit PHP, also mit PCRE. Beide lesen fast alles gleich, aber nicht
alles. Was nur JavaScript kennt, weist der Bau ab: \u-Escapes, [^], [], ein Lookbehind
unbegrenzter Länge. Was das PCRE des eigenen Rechners nicht lesen kann, meldet die Erzeugung der
Relay-Konfiguration (5.2). Am sichersten sind einfache Muster aus
Zeichenklassen und Wiederholungen.
Wer noch prüft

Der Bau prüft die Beschreibung: ob min unter max liegt, ob jede Option einen Wert hat, ob
ein Muster ein regulärer Ausdruck ist. Ein Fehler hält den Bau an (9.2).
Das Relay prüft jede Sendung noch einmal mit denselben Regeln, denn ein Browser lässt sich
umgehen. Weist es ein Feld ab, zeigt der Browser den Satz unter genau diesem Feld. Eine
verschlüsselte Sendung kann das Relay nicht lesen; es prüft dann nur, ob es ein PGP-Block der
erlaubten Größe ist.

forms/2-felder/03-breite-und-anordnung.title: 2.3 – Breite und Anordnung
forms/2-felder/03-breite-und-anordnung.content:
Ohne Angabe steht jedes Feld über die ganze Breite des Formulars, eines unter dem anderen. Zwei
Schlüssel ändern das.

width





















WertBreitefullDie ganze Zeile (Vorgabe).halfDie halbe Zeile. Zwei Felder stehen nebeneinander.thirdEin Drittel. Drei Felder stehen nebeneinander.
fields:
  - { type: text, name: first, label: Vorname, width: half }
  - { type: text, name: last, label: Nachname, width: half }
  - { type: text, name: zip, label: PLZ, width: third }
  - { type: text, name: city, label: Ort, width: third }
  - { type: text, name: country, label: Land, width: third }
Felder, die nicht in die Zeile passen, beginnen eine neue. Ein half neben einem third lässt
also eine Lücke.
Die Breite richtet sich nach dem Formular, nicht nach dem Fenster. Ein Formular in einer
schmalen Spalte ist auch auf einem großen Bildschirm schmal. Ist es schmaler als 32rem, wird aus
einem Drittel eine Hälfte; unter 22rem steht jedes Feld wieder über die ganze Zeile. Auf dem
Telefon ergibt das von selbst eine Spalte.
Das braucht Container-Queries (Chrome 105, Safari 16, Firefox 110). Ein älterer Browser zeigt
jedes Feld über die ganze Zeile.
layout: inline
Bei radio und checkboxes stellt layout: inline die Optionen nebeneinander. Sie brechen um,
wo die Zeile nicht reicht.
- type: radio
  name: reply
  label: Antwort per
  layout: inline
  options:
    - { value: email, label: E-Mail }
    - { value: phone, label: Telefon }
    - { value: post, label: Post }
Bei select wirkt es nicht, dessen Optionen sind ohnehin eine aufklappende Liste. Der Bau sagt
das.
